title: Designer, OpenAI.com
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI didn’t begin as a traditional company. It began as an idea: that artificial intelligence could be developed in a way that benefits everyone. As a creative team, our role is to help make sure the work behind that idea is understood, as it leaves the lab and meets the world.
This company works at the frontier of intelligence. Like any frontier, it’s unfinished, constantly shifting, and still being explored. Our job is to stay close to that uncertainty and help shape how this story gets told, in a way that feels grounded and human. We do this through campaigns, launches, films, brand systems, and work that doesn’t fit neatly into any of those categories yet. This team is for people who want to help shape something from the beginning.

About the Role

We’re looking for a designer to help shape OpenAI.com. This role is responsible for designing exceptional web experiences that bring our brand, mission, and products to life for a global audience. You’ll work closely with engineering, brand design, and marketing to build and evolve OpenAI.com into a world-class destination.

In this role, you will:

  • Design pages and user flows that help people explore OpenAI’s research, understand our products, and find what they need on OpenAI.com.

  • Work from early sketches and wireframes through interactive prototypes and high-fidelity designs, refining the work as you learn what’s clear and where people get stuck.

  • Shape the story of a page with writers, marketers, and brand designers, using layout, typography, and interaction to bring the content to life.

  • Partner with engineers through launch to refine how each experience looks, feels, and works across screen sizes, with attention to accessibility and performance.

  • Build on the web design system and work with brand and engineering to turn recurring design needs into reusable components and patterns.

  • Share work in progress, explain your design decisions, and give other designers specific feedback in critique.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

  • 8+ years of experience designing large-scale, consumer-facing websites or web products.

  • A knack for organizing complex information into pages and navigation that people can find their way around.

  • Experience working with engineers, marketers, writers, and brand designers to take web projects from concept to launch.

  • The ability to connect the purpose of a page to the details of its design, from the overall flow to typography, spacing, and interaction states.

  • Curiosity about OpenAI’s work and a willingness to share early ideas, seek feedback, and revise a design.

  • Experience designing for modern web technologies and content management systems.

  • An eye for when motion or a small interaction can help someone understand what’s changed or what to do next.

OpenAI’s mission is to build safe artificial general intelligence (AGI) which benefits all of humanity. This long-term undertaking brings the world’s best scientists, engineers, and business professionals into one lab together to accomplish this.

descriptionHtml:
About the team

OpenAI’s Applied AI organization turns our latest model capabilities into products used by hundreds of millions of consumers, developers, and organizations worldwide. Our teams build the product experiences and platform foundations behind ChatGPT, Codex, our API platform, and offerings for businesses, enterprises, educational institutions, and other customers.

Financial Engineering powers how customers purchase, access, and pay for these products. About the team

Life sciences is one of the clearest areas where advances in intelligence can meaningfully benefit the world at large. The OpenAI Life Sciences team works at the intersection of advancing frontier life sciences model capabilities and building products to help scientists accelerate their research and leverage the full potential of AI for scientific work.

We’re building platforms that connect model intelligence with practical scientific workflows. Our work covers workflows from next-gen sequencing analysis to designing new drugs, helping scientists run computational workloads as well as access laboratory services. By making these capabilities more accessible and useful, we aim to improve early discovery and support downstream progress in drug development.

We’re looking for experienced full-stack product engineers with strong backend skills to join our growing Life Sciences team.

You’ll help define products, design systems, and ship experiences that connect scientists with AI capabilities and laboratory workflows. title: EDA Cloud & Developer Infrastructure Engineer
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Hardware organization develops AI-native silicon and system-level solutions for the unique demands of advanced AI workloads. Building on efforts like Jalapeño, our custom silicon program, the team works across silicon architecture, RTL design, verification, physical design, systems software, and infrastructure to deliver highly performant, efficient, and scalable hardware solutions.

The Silicon & Systems team brings together hardware and software engineers to co-design and build the next generation of AI infrastructure. We operate at the intersection of silicon, systems, and software, tackling complex technical challenges across the full hardware development lifecycle, from early architecture and design through validation, deployment, and production.

About the Role

We’re looking for an Infrastructure Software Engineer to build and scale the infrastructure and developer workflows that power OpenAI’s custom silicon development. You’ll work closely with engineering teams across design verification, physical design, emulation, formal verification, and systems software to develop reliable, automated, and efficient workflows that accelerate hardware development.

In this role, you'll own and improve the cloud infrastructure, high-performance computing (HPC) environments, CI/CD pipelines, regression systems, and data platforms that support our silicon engineering teams. You'll translate complex hardware development requirements into scalable infrastructure solutions, reducing manual overhead, improving reliability, and enabling engineers to iterate faster.

This is a highly collaborative, hands-on role with opportunities to drive improvements across the entire hardware development lifecycle. We're looking for engineers who bring deep expertise in one or more infrastructure domains, strong software engineering fundamentals, and an interest in expanding their impact across the broader platform.

In this role, you will:

  • Build developer tools and workflows: Partner with hardware engineering teams to understand their development processes, identify bottlenecks, and build tooling, services, and APIs that automate workflows and accelerate engineering productivity.

  • Develop and scale regression infrastructure: Design, implement, and operate large-scale regression systems spanning job scheduling, execution, results collection, triage, and reporting, with a focus on performance, reliability, and reproducibility.

  • Own CI/CD infrastructure: Build and maintain automated pipelines for infrastructure, developer tooling, and cluster configurations, enabling safe deployments, testing, and continuous improvement.

  • Scale cloud and HPC environments: Design, provision, and operate cloud infrastructure and high-performance compute clusters, optimizing scheduling, capacity, reliability, and cost efficiency to support demanding silicon development workloads.

  • Build data infrastructure and observability: Develop data pipelines, databases, and monitoring systems that provide visibility into regression results, infrastructure health, resource utilization, and engineering efficiency.

  • Drive platform reliability and operational excellence: Troubleshoot complex infrastructure issues, improve monitoring and alerting, automate recovery processes, and build systems that are resilient, maintainable, and scalable.

  • Collaborate across hardware and software teams: Work directly with engineers across RTL, verification, physical design, emulation, and software to continuously improve the infrastructure supporting OpenAI's silicon development.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have strong software engineering fundamentals, with proficiency in Python or a similar programming language and experience building reliable automation, tools, or infrastructure services.

  • Bring deep technical expertise in at least one area of infrastructure engineering, such as Linux/HPC environments, cloud infrastructure, CI/CD systems, storage, networking, or EDA development workflows.

  • Have experience designing, deploying, and operating cloud infrastructure, preferably Azure, with familiarity in infrastructure-as-code tools such as Terraform or Bicep.

  • Have strong Linux systems knowledge, including processes, filesystems, networking, permissions, performance troubleshooting, and system administration.

  • Have experience building and maintaining CI/CD pipelines using tools such as Jenkins, Buildkite, GitHub Actions, or similar platforms.

  • Are comfortable debugging complex distributed infrastructure problems, identifying root causes, and implementing durable solutions.

  • Enjoy working closely with engineering teams to understand technical requirements and translate them into scalable, practical infrastructure solutions.

  • Take ownership of systems end to end, from initial design and implementation through deployment, monitoring, and ongoing operational improvements.

  • Bring strong technical judgment, clear communication, and a collaborative approach to solving ambiguous engineering challenges.

  • Are curious about hardware development and excited to expand your technical expertise across infrastructure, silicon design workflows, and developer productivity.

Bonus Qualifications

  • Experience supporting ASIC or semiconductor development environments, including EDA workflows, design verification, physical design, emulation, or formal verification.

  • Experience operating large-scale HPC clusters or workload schedulers such as Slurm.

  • Familiarity with compute farms, regression frameworks, build systems, and hardware development toolchains.

  • Experience with enterprise identity and authentication systems, such as Entra ID, OpenLDAP, FreeIPA, or SSSD.

  • Experience designing and operating relational databases such as PostgreSQL or MySQL, including schema design, migrations, query optimization, and backups.

  • Familiarity with distributed systems components, including message queues, caching layers, artifact storage, and backend services.

  • Experience with high-performance storage systems, data movement optimization, or large-scale compute infrastructure.

  • Experience managing EDA license servers, license utilization, or other shared infrastructure resources in hardware development environments.

title: Performance Modeling Engineer ~2
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Hardware organization develops system and infrastructure solutions designed for the unique demands of advanced AI workloads. We work closely with architecture, infrastructure, and vendor teams to evaluate system performance and guide critical design decisions.

Our team focuses on building and applying performance modeling frameworks to understand system behavior, quantify tradeoffs, and support next-generation infrastructure design.

About the Role

We are seeking an Performance Modeling Engineer to support the development and application of modeling tools used to evaluate AI system performance and inform architectural decisions.

In this role, you will partner closely with Senior Performance Modeling Engineers and the Performance Modeling Lead to analyze system behavior, run simulations and analytical models, and help evaluate tradeoffs across compute, memory, networking, and storage. You will contribute to building modeling frameworks while developing a strong foundation in system architecture and AI infrastructure.

This role is ideal for early-career engineers with 1–2 years of experience in software engineering, systems analysis, or performance modeling who are excited to grow in large-scale infrastructure and hardware/software systems.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance.

Key Responsibilities

  • Support the development and maintenance of performance modeling tools and frameworks

  • Assist in building models to evaluate system behavior across compute, memory, networking, and interconnect subsystems

  • Help analyze distributed system scaling behavior and identify performance bottlenecks

title: Researcher, Recursive Self-Improvement Safety
descriptionHtml:
About the team

Models are becoming increasingly capable—moving from tools that assist humans to agents that can plan, execute, and adapt in the real world. Mitigating the frontier risks resulting from these capabilities is paramount to OpenAI’s ability to continue deploying models safely.

The Preparedness team is dedicated to addressing these critical risks. Our work includes:

  1. Measurement. Monitoring and predicting the evolving capabilities of frontier AI systems.

  2. Mitigation. Keeping misalignment safeguards, alignment tools, and on track to adequately address extreme threats that might arise in the future.

  3. Coordination. Setting mitigation targets by maintaining OpenAI’s preparedness framework, and partnering with other staff to achieve these targets.

This is urgent, fast-paced work that has far-reaching implications for the company and for society.

About the role

Preparedness is hiring strong technical executors to support preparations for accelerated AI development, which may culminate in recursive self-improvement. This work relies on anticipating misalignment risks that might exist in the future, but might not exist now; so it’s especially important that people in this role are tasteful and strategic.

The role is wide-ranging, covering any mitigation for loss of control risk, spanning the design and implementation of better pre-deployment risk-assessment, control measures, RSI-relevant training interventions, and turning one’s technical work into established institutional practices and external-facing communications.

Below is a subset of our focus areas:

  • Scalable oversight: Establishing practices for model misbehavior monitoring and oversight which remain effective in superhuman model capability regimes, with a focus on bridging from today’s monitoring approaches to future-proof ones.

  • Automated auditing: As model capabilities increase, we’ll increasingly rely on automated approaches for finding the most severe forms of model misalignments. We’ll both need to sift through large swaths of production traffic to find the most egregious misalignments, and reliably elicit tail risks before deployment.

  • Rigorous monitorability: Rigorous testing and red-teaming of our measurements of model misbehavior related to loss-of-control (e.g. reward hacking, sandbagging, scheming). This includes better understanding monitorability, and e.g. preparing for potential losses of Chain-of-Thought monitorability.

  • Model behavior science: Design experiments and evaluations to understand the extent to which models are problematically misaligned, or their safety-relevant capabilities lag behind dangerous capabilities. This may include training model organisms of misbehavior for behaviors not currently present in production, or training interventions to increase safety-relevant capabilities.

  • Coordination and verification: Prototype technical mechanisms for verifying compliance with potential future AI safety agreements.

  • AI R&D risk measurement: Track progress toward automation of technical staff to inform OpenAI’s near-term investments in alignment and security.

  • Maintaining and strengthening RSI safety cases: We’re especially interested in identifying and addressing blindspots of mitigation areas which we may have missed.

Generally, our team alternates between performing rigorous hypothesis-driven research and turning our insights into interventions or control systems which impact production models, with occasional support of engineering teams.

In this role, you will:

  • Carefully consider the problems OpenAI might face in the future and how to prepare for them.

  • Turn an open-ended objective like “prepare for future misalignment threats” into a much more concrete direction (e.g. “stress-test monitors for scheming”) – prioritizing the work that is most useful to start right now.

  • Execute quickly, building scrappy prototypes, and then improving them iteratively until they become established components of our safety pipelines.

  • Secure buy-in from other staff at OpenAI when necessary, and communicate your work clearly.

  • Collaborate with or manage other staff as needed, since we might need to rapidly scale to tackle these problems quickly.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Are an exceptional technical executor.

  • Have strong strategic and research taste: you can prioritize effectively in domains with weak feedback loops.

  • Are passionate about mitigating the risks associated with recursive self-improvement.

  • Are driven by a desire to do whatever work most positively impacts the future of AI development.

  • Bonus: you have already done work in one of the domains listed above (ML research, AI alignment, AI verification etc).

title: Physical Design Engineer
descriptionHtml:
About the Team
OpenAI’s Hardware organization develops AI-native silicon and system-level solutions for the unique demands of advanced AI workloads. Building on efforts like Jalapeño, the team is developing future generations of AI-native silicon and tightly integrated systems to power the next generation of frontier models. By co-designing chips, systems, tools, and methodologies, the team helps deliver faster, more efficient, and production-ready hardware for OpenAI’s supercomputing platform.

About the Role
 We are seeking a highly skilled Physical Design Engineer with deep expertise in physical design and methodology. This individual contributor role sits within our physical design team and is central to delivering power, performance, and area (PPA) optimized datapath and interconnect solutions for next-generation AI accelerators.

You’ll work closely with RTL designers to define and execute on physical design strategies. You will develop tools, flows and methodologies to increase team productivity. Your work will directly impact silicon’s performance and cost efficiency, as well as the team’s execution velocity and quality.

In this role, you will:

  • Develop, build and own tools, flows and methodologies for physical implementation

  • Own physical implementation of floorplan blocks from floorplanning to final signoff

  • Collaborate with RTL designers to drive optimal block implementation solutions

  • Analyze and optimize design for timing, power, and area trade-offs, working in collaboration with EDA vendors and ASIC partners

Qualifications:

  • BS w/ 4+ or MS with 2+ years or PhD with 0-1 year(s) of relevant industry experience in physical design and methodology development

  • Demonstrated success in taping out complex silicon designs

  • Hands-on experience with block physical implementation and PPA convergence

  • Strong coding experience with python, bazel, TCL

  • Strong experience building physical design tools, flows and methodologies

  • Strong understanding of microarchitecture, RTL design, physical design, circuit design, physical verification and timing closure.

  • Deep familiarity with industry-standard tools and flows for physical synthesis, PNR, LEC and power estimation

Bonus:

  • Experience with AI or HPC-focused chips

  • Experience with optimizing PPA for high performance compute cores

title: HRBP, Tech
descriptionHtml:
About this Team

The HR Business Partner (HRBP) team at OpenAI partners with leaders on complex organizational and talent decisions where the right path is not always obvious. We stay close enough to the business to understand how it works and focus our time on the decisions that benefit most from our judgment, context, and influence.

We work with urgency, empathy, and sound judgment. We value sincerity, intellectual honesty, and collaboration over ego.

About this Role

As a Senior HR Business Partner supporting Tech, you’ll partner with leaders in engineering, product, and other technical teams as they build and scale their organizations. You’ll get close enough to the work to understand what’s slowing teams down, then help leaders make decisions about structure, talent, and how teams work together as technical priorities evolve.

This is an individual contributor role reporting to an HRBP Lead. You’ll advise senior leaders on complex decisions and work directly with managers to make those decisions stick.

In this role, you will:

  • Translate technical priorities into org and talent decisions. Help leaders decide what capabilities to build, how to structure teams, and where ownership needs to sit.

  • Diagnose what’s getting in the way of team performance. Use data and input from the people doing the work to separate structural issues from problems with roles, priorities, or how teams work together.

  • Develop technical leaders. Coach managers through performance, growth, and succession decisions, and help them set clear expectations for both people managers and individual contributors.

  • Lead change as technical priorities shift. Help leaders think through the impact of reorganizations or changes in ownership and communicate decisions clearly to the teams affected.

  • Build People practices that work for technical teams. Partner with fellow HRBPs and People specialists to adapt performance, development, and talent processes without adding unnecessary overhead.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

  • 7–10+ years of HR experience, including at least 5 years as an HR Business Partner in a high-growth or complex environment.

  • Experience partnering with engineering, product, or other technical organizations, and curiosity about how technical teams make decisions and deliver work.

  • A track record of helping technical leaders navigate org design, workforce planning, or talent decisions as teams grow or priorities change.

The work combines rapid experimentation with the demands of established products: complex systems, real users, and high expectations for quality and performance. You will combine deep technical judgment, hands-on engineering, and customer leadership to take ambitious ideas from use-case selection and architecture through prototyping, evaluation, production launch, and scale.   • Scale the Applied AI Engineer function through sharing knowledge and publishing best-practices to our internal and external repositories.

title: Researcher, Safety - Frontier Assurance
descriptionHtml:
About the team

The Frontier Assurance team strengthens OpenAI’s safety decisions through independent expertise, rigorous assessment, and public transparency. We coordinate external evaluations of frontier models and safeguards, develop approaches such as embedded auditing, and manage the misalignment disclosure process and safeguard testing. Our work helps independent experts scrutinize OpenAI’s safety approach and ensures their findings inform consequential decisions about advanced AI systems.

About the role

As a researcher on Frontier Assurance, you will build the technical foundations for rigorous assessments of frontier AI risks. You will help design technical assessments with external evaluators and internal teams: identify consequential safety claims to test, define the evidence and methods needed to assess them, and address gaps in coverage.

You will work closely with external evaluators and embedded auditors, helping them understand the systems they are assessing and access the models, data, and technical information their work requires. Where direct access is not possible, you will conduct experiments and analyses on their behalf, with methods and results they can meaningfully scrutinize.

This role combines research engineering, experimental design, and close technical collaboration. You will move between investigating specific safety questions, navigating complex internal systems, and building reusable tools that make assessments more thorough and efficient. Your work will help turn independent scrutiny into concrete evidence about model capabilities, safeguards, and remaining risks.

In this role, you will:

  • Help design assessments with external evaluators and internal teams: identify consequential safety claims to test, define the evidence and methods needed to assess them, and address gaps in coverage.

  • Support the technical execution of third-party assessments and embedded audits focused on frontier risks, working with evaluators to translate research questions into experiments, analyses, and evidence requirements.

  • Pair closely with external researchers to provide the data, technical documentation, and context needed to assess models and safeguards. Help them understand relevant system behavior, configurations, and limitations.

  • Design and implement secure access to assessment environments, working with research, engineering, and security teams to make relevant models, tools, and information available.

  • Conduct experiments and run analyses on evaluators’ behalf when direct access is constrained. Develop methods collaboratively, document implementation choices, and make results reproducible and open to challenge.

  • Build tooling that automates auditing, assessment workflows, and internal assurance work, including evidence collection, evaluation execution, and tracking changes across model or safeguard versions.

  • Reproduce external findings, investigate discrepancies with internal results, and work with relevant teams to test proposed mitigations and identify unresolved questions.

  • Document methods, findings, and limitations clearly so that evaluators and internal decision-makers can understand what the evidence establishes and where uncertainty remains.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have strong software engineering skills and experience building research tools, evaluation infrastructure, or systems for analyzing complex data.

  • Have practical experience working with modern machine learning systems, including designing experiments, running evaluations, and interpreting results.

  • Can navigate unfamiliar codebases and infrastructure, debug across system boundaries, and turn ambiguous research requests into reliable technical implementations.

  • Bring sound judgment to experimental design and measurement, including identifying confounders, limitations, and gaps in evidence.

  • Enjoy working closely with researchers, explaining technical systems, and helping others investigate difficult questions.

  • Value independent scrutiny and can support rigorous assessments that challenge internal assumptions.

  • Have an understanding of, or strong interest in, frontier AI risks, alignment, and the evaluation of safeguards.

Experience with AI safety evaluations, adversarial testing, security research, or technical auditing would be especially relevant.

title: Strategic Technology Negotiations Lead
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI's Strategic Sourcing team helps the company scale responsibly, efficiently, and at speed. We partner with leaders across Engineering, Research, IT, Systems, Finance, Legal, and other teams to shape commercial strategies, negotiate critical agreements, and build resilient supplier ecosystems. Our work connects technical strategy, commercial judgment, financial discipline, and execution in support of OpenAI's mission.

About the Role

OpenAI is seeking a Strategic Technology Negotiations Lead to personally lead some of the company's most complex and consequential technology negotiations.

This is not a people manager role. It is a senior strategic IC operator role for an expert negotiator who wants to remain close to the work and personally drive high-impact outcomes. We are especially interested in leaders who have managed teams and are intentionally seeking an individual contributor role where their impact comes through judgment, influence, and direct ownership.

Rather than owning a fixed category, you will be deployed against high-priority opportunities where deal complexity, commercial stakes, executive visibility, or time pressure require exceptional negotiation leadership. Your initial focus will include data platforms and infrastructure, including data lake and lakehouse technologies, observability, and enterprise SaaS, with flexibility to work across other strategic technology areas. You will lead negotiations from strategy through execution, aligning decision-makers and driving agreements to closure.

Many of these negotiations exist within broader supplier and partner ecosystems. You will look beyond the immediate transaction to account for interconnected cost, equity, revenue, partnership, risk, and long-term strategic implications. Success requires strong economics, sound judgment under pressure, executive credibility, and the ability to bring stakeholders with you through difficult decisions.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

  • Personally lead complex, high-value, and business-critical technology negotiations from initial strategy through signed agreement.

  • Develop fact-based negotiation plans that define objectives, leverage, alternatives, sequencing, roles, decision points, and escalation paths.

  • Rapidly synthesize technical requirements, supplier economics, market dynamics, adoption patterns, dependencies, and business priorities.

  • Partner with leaders across Engineering, Research, IT, Systems, Finance, Legal, Corporate Development, and other teams to establish a unified negotiation strategy.

  • Assess each negotiation within the broader supplier ecosystem, identifying interconnected relationships that may create value, constraints, dependencies, or leverage.

  • Shape complex deal structures with cost, equity, revenue, partnership, risk, and long-term strategic implications.

  • Advise executives through clear, decision-ready narratives covering deal strategy, financial impact, alternatives, risks, tradeoffs, and recommendations.

  • Lead supplier engagement at working-team and executive levels, including difficult escalations and negotiations conducted under significant pressure.

  • Create commercial structures that deliver meaningful savings and cost avoidance while improving scalability, flexibility, performance, and risk allocation.

  • Turn lessons from major negotiations into reusable playbooks, market intelligence, and stronger negotiation practices for Strategic Sourcing.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have 10+ years of experience leading complex commercial negotiations in strategic sourcing, technology procurement, strategic partnerships, deal strategy, corporate development, or a related field.

  • Are an expert negotiator who enjoys personally developing the strategy, leading the room, and driving difficult deals to resolution.

  • Have previously managed or led teams and are intentionally seeking a senior individual contributor role centered on direct ownership, influence, and execution.

  • Have personally led large-scale enterprise software or technology agreements with sophisticated pricing, commitment, licensing, consumption, or partnership structures.

  • Understand enterprise software business models, including usage-based pricing, multi-year commitments, ramp structures, pooled consumption, growth protections, and performance-based economics.

title: Applied AI Architect (Brazil)
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The AI Architect team partners with organizations to turn OpenAI's most capable models into meaningful, real-world impact. We work with customers across industries and digital-native businesses to identify where AI can create value, design secure and scalable solutions, and help those solutions move from early exploration into sustained production adoption. The team brings together technical strategy, customer partnership, and practical deployment expertise, working closely with Sales, Product, Engineering, Research, and specialist delivery teams.

About the Role

As an AI Architect, you will be the senior technical owner for a named portfolio of customers and the primary technical counterpart to their leadership teams. You will act as the “CTO of your book of business”, shaping each customer's AI strategy and guiding their journey from pre-sales discovery and solution evaluation through deployment, adoption, and measurable business impact.

You will own the technical account plan across ChatGPT Enterprise, the OpenAI API, Codex, and other agentic AI solutions. In partnership with the Account Director, you will translate business priorities into a focused use-case portfolio, an actionable adoption roadmap, and a clear path to durable customer value and growth. The Account Director owns commercial strategy; you own the technical strategy, customer journey, and path to production value.

You will remain accountable for the technical outcome while bringing in the right specialists across deployment, implementation, enablement, security, product, and partners to provide deeper expertise and execute work where needed. This role calls for strong industry fluency, sound architectural judgment, and the ability to move confidently between executive strategy and hands-on technical conversations.

In this role, you will:

  • Serve as the primary technical advisor and long-term technical relationship owner for a named portfolio of existing customers and pre-sales prospects.

  • Partner with Account Directors on account strategy while owning the technical account plan, technical milestones, adoption priorities, and expansion opportunities.

  • Lead discovery with executives and technical teams to identify, qualify, and prioritize use cases tied to meaningful business outcomes.

  • Develop clear Applied AI Architectures spanning models, applications, data, integration, security, privacy, governance, evaluation, and deployment.

  • Guide customers through technical evaluations, demonstrations, workshops, prototypes, and proofs of value, securing confidence in both the solution and its path to production.

  • Maintain a focused use-case portfolio with clear decision criteria, ownership, blockers, success measures, delivery needs, and adoption plans.

  • Develop trusted relationships and technical champions across CTOs, CIOs, CISOs, AI leaders, engineering teams, and other customer stakeholders.

  • Qualify and coordinate support from Deployment Engineering, implementation, training and enablement, product and domain specialists, partners, and other delivery teams.

  • Remain accountable for technical progress and customer outcomes while ensuring delivery teams own implementation execution once engaged.

  • Track adoption, usage, account health, production readiness, and measurable customer impact, intervening early when risks threaten value realization.

  • Apply industry or digital-native expertise to recognize repeatable patterns, sharpen customer priorities, and identify relevant expansion opportunities.

  • Share customer insights with Product, Engineering, and Research, translating field learnings into better products, architecture guidance, and reusable practices.

You might thrive in this role if you:

descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Client Platform Engineering (CPE) team delivers trusted devices at scale: secure by default, reliable by design, and effortless to use. We own platform capabilities across macOS, Windows, iOS, Android, and Linux, spanning endpoint posture and device trust, application delivery, onboarding, updates, telemetry, workflow orchestration, and employee-facing remediation. The team partners deeply with Security, Research, Applied, and specialized engineering groups to enable and protect OpenAI while reducing friction for the people advancing our mission.

About the Role

As an Engineering Manager for CPE, you will lead a team of engineers responsible for the strategy, delivery, and operation of OpenAI’s cross-platform client foundation. You will combine people leadership with strong technical judgment: setting direction, developing engineers, reviewing architecture and tradeoffs, and creating the operating mechanisms that turn ambiguous needs into durable platform outcomes. This is a high-leverage role at the intersection of security, reliability, developer velocity, and employee experience.

CPE is a highly technical platform engineering organization delivering first-party services, automation, observability, and safe fleet operations. We’re looking for a leader who can guide its next chapter, scaling the team and its systems, partnering across the company, and raising the bar for secure, reliable, low-friction experiences across every supported platform.

title: Software Engineer, Platform Systems
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The Platform Systems team at OpenAI operates at the intersection of cutting-edge AI and large-scale distributed systems. We build the engineering and research infrastructure required to train OpenAI’s flagship models on some of the world’s largest, custom-built supercomputers.

Our team develops core model training software and works deep in the stack - spanning collective communication, compute efficiency, parallelism strategies, fault tolerance, failure detection, and observability. The systems we build are foundational to OpenAI’s research velocity, enabling reliable, efficient training at frontier scale.

We collaborate closely with researchers across the organization, continuously incorporating learnings from across OpenAI into the evolution of our training platform.

About the Role

As a Software Engineer, Platform Systems, you will design and build distributed systems that provide visibility into large-scale training workloads and help operate them reliably at scale.

You’ll work on failure detection, tracing, and observability systems that identify slow or faulty nodes, surface performance bottlenecks, and help engineers understand and optimize massive distributed training jobs. This infrastructure is critical to operating OpenAI’s training stack and is actively evolving to support new use cases and increasingly complex workloads.

This role sits at the core of our training infrastructure, blending systems engineering, performance analysis, and large-scale debugging.

In This Role, You Will

title: Research Scientist / Research Engineer, Safety + Alignment, Search
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The Foundations Research team works on high-risk, high-reward ideas that could shape the next decade of AI. Our goal is to advance the science and data that enable our training and scaling efforts, with a particular focus on future frontier models. We push the boundaries of data, scaling laws, optimization techniques, model architectures, model + search co-design and efficiency improvements to propel our science.

The Search team sits within Foundations, building agentic search by co-designing model-system interfaces with the core search stack: serving, indexing, and retrieval. We research and develop large-scale systems that transform and index vast corpora, enabling models to most effectively find and reason over information. In close partnership with researchers, we bring modeling advances into production and improve how AI systems discover, retrieve, and use knowledge.

About the Role

We’re looking for a Researcher to lead our safety and alignment research: building the systems that distinguish useful web content from spam, manipulation, and other adversarial or low-quality material.

The challenge extends beyond evaluating individual pages. A page may appear credible in isolation, while its links, metadata, or relationships with other sites reveal coordinated manipulation. As AI makes convincing content easier to produce at scale, detection systems must adapt to increasingly sophisticated adversaries.

You’ll define the technical approach, build classifiers and evaluations, and shape how integrity signals influence what Search indexes and retrieves. Working closely with Search and broader Safety and Integrity teams, you’ll use frontier models to advance detection methods and bring them into production.

Responsibilities

  • Define the technical direction for Safety + Integrity, identifying gaps and determining which problems and interventions to prioritize.

  • Develop AI and ML systems to detect spam, scams, phishing, malicious domains, prompt injections, and other adversarial or low-quality web content.

  • Discover useful signals across page content, links, domains, metadata, and relationships between websites, including patterns that reveal coordinated manipulation.

  • Build evaluations that measure detection quality and how integrity interventions affect the information Search surfaces.

  • Translate detection signals into indexing, ranking, and filtering decisions, improving what models can retrieve and rely on.

  • Serve as the technical owner for integrity within Search, partnering with researchers, engineers, and broader Safety and Integrity teams to build and deploy these systems.

You Might Thrive in This Role If You Have

  • Deep experience in web spam, search quality, adversarial content detection, or related integrity problems at scale.

  • Strong applied ML and research skills, with experience developing classifiers, detection methods, and evaluations for real-world systems.

  • An understanding of how adversaries manipulate content and links, coordinate across sites, and adapt to detection systems.

  • A track record of independently defining ambiguous technical problems and driving solutions from experimentation through production.

  • Experience working across research, engineering, and integrity teams while remaining hands-on with technical work.

  • A first-principles approach to using frontier models and compute, and a strong interest in keeping detection systems effective as adversaries evolve.

title: Privacy Operations Analyst
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

Regulatory & Privacy Operations sits within User Safety & Risk Operations (USRO), part of OpenAI’s broader User Operations organization. We build and run the operational programs that protect user rights and support OpenAI’s legal, regulatory & privacy obligations across its products and developer tools.

We partner with Legal, Privacy Engineering, Product, Policy, Governance, Risk & Compliance, Support Operations, and external vendors to resolve sensitive cases and build reliable, scalable operations. Our remit spans privacy, online safety, AI regulation, and intellectual property.

About the Role

We are seeking an experienced Privacy Operations Analyst to own and evolve our global Privacy Operations workstream from Dublin. This individual contributor role combines hands-on management of complex privacy matters with accountability for operational health, vendor quality, and program improvement.

You will take end-to-end ownership of how privacy rights requests are received, assessed, routed, and resolved across a tiered operating model. You will partner closely with Privacy Legal, the Data Protection Officer’s office, Privacy Engineering, and operations teams to translate legal guidance into practical workflows and resolve issues that cross organizational boundaries.

Beyond keeping operations healthy, you will set priorities and deliver improvements that reduce avoidable demand, strengthen controls, and enable safe automation. We are looking for someone who independently identifies problems, makes sound decisions with incomplete information, and carries work from diagnosis through implementation and measurable results.

Privacy will be your primary remit. You will also develop sufficient familiarity with adjacent Regulatory Operations workflows to recognize intersecting risks and provide secondary support when priorities require it.

In This Role, You Will

  • Own global Privacy Operations across intake, identity verification, case handling, escalations, and closure, including access, deletion, export, correction, and opt-out requests, working within guidance agreed with Legal.

  • Independently investigate and resolve complex or sensitive privacy cases, including third-party requests, account restrictions, and complaints about personal information in AI outputs. Recognize when legal interpretation or technical investigation is needed and coordinate the right partners through resolution.

  • Own operational health across internal and vendor-supported queues. Use demand forecasts, backlog age, response and resolution times, quality, and capacity data to identify emerging risks and act before deadlines or user outcomes deteriorate.

  • Drive vendor performance through clear procedures, training, quality calibration, escalation criteria, and corrective actions. Expand delegated handling where appropriate, with the controls and evidence needed to maintain quality.

  • Build and deliver a prioritized roadmap for workflow simplification, self-service, tooling, and AI-assisted automation. Define requirements, evaluate accuracy and failure modes, establish human review and escalation safeguards, and measure impact after launch.

  • Translate privacy requirements and Legal guidance into standard operating procedures, decision trees, case documentation, and operational controls. Keep guidance current as products, policies, and requirements evolve.

  • Lead Privacy Operations readiness for product launches and policy changes. Assess likely demand, new case types, routing, capacity, and dependencies, and drive practical mitigations with cross-functional owners.

  • Investigate handling failures and recurring complaints, establish root causes and wider exposure, and deliver corrective actions with clear ownership and evidence of effectiveness.

  • Maintain reliable reporting and case records to support audit readiness, control testing, and Legal-led responses to regulatory inquiries. Communicate the risk, impact, recommendation, and decisions needed clearly to partners and leadership.

  • Set priorities across immediate casework and longer-term improvements, make explicit trade-offs, and influence partners across teams and time zones to deliver results.

You Might Thrive in This Role If You

  • Have 8+ years of relevant experience in privacy operations, regulatory operations, legal operations, or a related field, with substantial hands-on ownership of privacy rights workflows in a global technology environment.

  • Have a strong working understanding of GDPR, CCPA/CPRA, and privacy rights operations, and can translate counsel’s guidance into consistent, usable processes. You understand the challenges of identity verification, sensitive data handling, and complex request fulfillment.

  • Have independently owned a complex operational program, set its priorities, and delivered improvements across multiple teams, with evidence of better quality, lower risk, faster resolution, or reduced manual work.

  • Have managed vendor-supported operations and tiered escalation models, including service levels, quality assurance, capacity planning, training, and performance remediation.

  • Bring an automation-first approach grounded in sound risk judgment. You can identify what should be automated, define how it will be evaluated, and retain appropriate oversight for sensitive decisions.

  • Are comfortable using operational data, dashboards, and case analysis to diagnose problems, test assumptions, and make recommendations. You can distinguish a temporary volume spike from a systemic process or control failure.

  • Communicate clearly and concisely, including on sensitive cases and operational risks. Your updates explain what matters, what has changed, and what action or decision is needed.

  • Exercise strong judgment in ambiguity, act with urgency proportionate to risk, and know when to decide independently and when to escalate. You follow through without relying on detailed direction.

  • Build effective relationships with Legal, Engineering, Product, and operations partners, and can influence decisions without formal authority.

Additional Experience That Would Be Valuable

  • Experience with privacy operations for AI products, including requests involving model outputs or personal information.

  • Practical experience with tooling, automation evaluation, or AI-assisted quality assurance.

  • Familiarity with adjacent frameworks such as the DSA, OSA, or EU AI Act, and experience supporting audits or regulatory inquiries.

  • A relevant privacy qualification, such as CIPP/E or CIPM.

title: Deal Operations, AMER
descriptionHtml:
About the Role

OpenAI is seeking a senior individual contributor to support revenue growth across the Americas (AMER) by helping sales teams structure and close commercially sound deals. You will balance speed and responsiveness with pricing discipline, consistent processes, and appropriate financial and commercial controls.

In this role, you will be the day-to-day Deal Operations partner for AMER account teams, reviewing pricing, discounts, and commercial terms across new business, renewals, and expansions. You will guide sellers through deal requirements, evaluate non-standard requests, and coordinate the approvals needed to move opportunities through contracting and closure.

You will also develop scalable workflows, guidance, and tools that improve deal turnaround times, documentation quality, and consistency across the region.

This role partners closely with Sales, Finance, Legal, Pricing, and Revenue Operations, with Product and other teams engaged as needed, to resolve deal issues and support accurate execution from quote through contract and booking.

In this role, you will:

  • Serve as the primary Deal Operations contact for AMER account teams, managing deal intake, prioritizing requests, and guiding sellers through pricing, review, and approval processes.

  • Review quotes and proposed commercial terms, including discounts, payment schedules, contract duration, and customer commitments, for accuracy and alignment with pricing guidelines and commercial policies.

  • Build financial analyses and deal models to assess revenue, margin, discount impact, and profitability, and explain the tradeoffs of proposed deal structures to decision-makers.

  • Partner with Sales to structure deals that meet customer needs and OpenAI’s commercial objectives, recommending alternatives when proposed terms fall outside established guidelines.

  • Coordinate deal reviews and required approvals across Finance, Legal, Pricing, and Revenue Operations. Prepare clear recommendations, document decisions, and escalate exceptions to the appropriate stakeholders.

  • Identify risks in non-standard terms and work with Legal and Finance to resolve contractual, billing, and revenue recognition considerations before execution.

  • Maintain complete deal records and approval documentation in CRM, CPQ, and contract management systems, and partner with Revenue Operations to align approved terms, executed agreements, and booking information.

  • Help develop and maintain deal approval policies, escalation paths, pricing guidance, and standardized templates. Improve workflows to reduce bottlenecks while maintaining appropriate controls.

  • Equip sellers with practical guidance and training on deal requirements and approval processes. Apply AI and automation to improve deal intake, knowledge retrieval, and self-service support.

  • Track Deal Desk metrics such as turnaround time, approval bottlenecks, exception trends, and quote accuracy. Use recurring deal patterns to recommend improvements to commercial policies, processes, and tools.

You Might Thrive in This Role If You Have:

  • 8+ years of experience in Deal Desk, commercial finance, pricing, sales operations, or a related function, preferably in a high-growth technology environment.

  • Hands-on experience reviewing and structuring complex enterprise deals and supporting quoting, commercial approvals, and contracting processes.

  • Strong financial modeling and analytical skills, including experience assessing pricing, discounts, revenue, margins, and deal profitability.

  • Knowledge of enterprise software commercial terms and subscription or consumption-based business models, with the judgment to identify issues that require Legal or Finance review.

  • Strong communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to explain commercial tradeoffs, make clear recommendations, and coordinate timely decisions across teams.

  • Experience with CRM systems, configure-price-quote (CPQ) tools, and contract management platforms, along with strong spreadsheet skills.

  • Attention to detail and a track record of improving approval workflows, documentation, and operational processes as a business scales.

  • Sound commercial judgment and the ability to manage competing priorities and tight deadlines while maintaining accuracy and appropriate controls.

  • A collaborative, hands-on approach to supporting sales teams and familiarity with using AI and automation to improve deal workflows and productivity.

title: Network Infrastructure Lead
descriptionHtml:
About the Role

Lead OpenAI’s site network infrastructure delivery, coordinating the physical installation and readiness of network systems with the central network team and contracted installation providers.

You will be OpenAI’s accountable on-site lead for physical network infrastructure construction and deployment, directing and overseeing the work of general contractors, specialist contractors and other service providers within your discipline. You will combine practical subject-matter depth with hands-on field leadership, managing contracted support to deliver safe, high-quality work to the integrated construction plan.

Reporting and scope

Report to the Site Construction Manager, who reports through the applicable project-management leadership. Maintain functional alignment with the Network Infrastructure leader and central network engineering team.

Own day-to-day discipline execution and contractor performance within the assigned site scope and delegated authority. Coordinate priorities and interfaces through the Site Construction Manager; escalate material cost, schedule, design and acceptance decisions to the appropriate owners.

This is a senior site delivery role, suited to an experienced superintendent, supervisor, manager or trade lead. Accountability is for an assigned discipline and site work packages. Site assignment, duration and any shared coverage follow project phase, workload and the staffing plan; effective on-site coverage is required during critical activities.

Key Responsibilities

  • Manage structured-cabling contractors, fiber installers, network installation partners and other service providers against the site delivery plan.

  • Translate approved network designs into executable field packages and coordinate bills of materials, material availability and installation sequencing with the central network team.

  • Oversee pathways, duct banks and building-entry interfaces, fiber and copper cabling, racks, patching, labeling and network-equipment installation as applicable.

  • Direct fiber and cabling quality assurance, review test results and traceability, and drive correction of defective or incomplete installations.

  • Coordinate power, cooling, space and physical access readiness with electrical, mechanical and CSLA leads and hardware deployment teams.

  • Coordinate network provisioning, connectivity validation and handover with authorized network engineering and operations teams; maintain accurate installation and as-built records.

  • Set clear contractor deliverables and work priorities; review staffing, progress and quality, identify constraints early, and drive recovery actions through the Site Construction Manager.

  • Provide concise progress and risk reporting, evaluate field impacts of proposed changes, and maintain accountable handoffs between construction partners and OpenAI teams.

Qualifications

  • Typically 8–10 years of large-scale data center network deployment, structured cabling, physical-layer installation or infrastructure delivery, with demonstrated field and contractor leadership. Equivalent depth of practical delivery experience will be considered.

  • Strong understanding of physical data center network topologies, network components, bills of materials, rack constraints and installation sequencing; translate approved designs into executable field plans.

  • Deep practical knowledge of fiber and copper plant installation, trunks, panels, terminations, cleaning, labeling and cable administration, including routing diversity and pathway separation.

  • Ability to oversee and assess port-to-port verification, continuity, optical power and optical time-domain reflectometer (OTDR) testing; troubleshoot field installation and mapping discrepancies and verify remediation.

  • Experience defining contractor work packages and statements of work, evaluating delivery requirements, forecasting labor needs and tracking quality, throughput, cost drivers and schedule performance within delegated authority.

  • Experience coordinating deployment prerequisites with engineering and construction teams and completing formal operations handover with as-builts, port maps, test evidence and clear ownership transfer.

  • Comfort with ticket-based execution, change control, incident escalation and documentation workflows that make network installation repeatable and auditable.

  • Demonstrated ability to lead contractors and service providers through changing site conditions, set clear deliverables and acceptance criteria, and resolve performance gaps across organizations without relying on direct reporting authority.

  • Strong written and verbal communication: maintain accurate field records, action and decision logs, and explain technical risks, schedule impacts and recovery options to site leadership, engineers and delivery partners.

  • Sound judgment when information is incomplete: identify assumptions, prerequisites and interfaces, determine what work can proceed within approved authority, and escalate unresolved risks before they affect safety, quality or delivery.

  • Relevant trade, apprenticeship, technical or degree-based preparation, or equivalent practical experience. Demonstrated field leadership and subject-matter competence are central to this site role.

About the Team

The mission of the Applied AI Engineering team is to enable the secure and impactful implementation of Agentic solutions. You’ll partner with their technical teams, subject matter experts, regional cloud providers, systems integrators, and implementation partners to move from prototype through production. title: Incident Commander, Detection & Response - US
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

Security is at the foundation of OpenAI’s mission to ensure that artificial general intelligence benefits all of humanity.

The Security team protects OpenAI’s technology, people, and products. We are technical in what we build but are operational in how we do our work, and are committed to supporting all products and research at OpenAI. Our Security team tenets include: prioritizing for impact, enabling researchers, preparing for future transformative technologies, and engaging a robust security culture.

About the Role

As an Incident Commander on Detection & Response, you’ll lead the response to complex security incidents affecting OpenAI’s intellectual property, customer data, and infrastructure. You’ll establish response priorities, coordinate technical work streams, drive containment and recovery decisions within agreed authority, and keep stakeholders informed as facts evolve. You’ll work with security and infrastructure teams across endpoints, identity, cloud, and compute environments, maintaining clear ownership and effective handoffs across time zones. Detection engineering knowledge is a supporting requirement: you’ll use telemetry and detection logic to assess evidence, identify visibility gaps, and guide improvements that make incident response more effective.

In this role, you will:

  • Run incident command from initial assessment through containment, recovery, and closure, establishing severity, scope, response objectives, and escalation needs.

  • Assign work stream owners and coordinate investigation, containment, and recovery in parallel. Maintain a decision log and distinguish confirmed facts from assumptions.

  • Drive timely containment and recovery decisions with the appropriate owners, weighing security risk, evidence preservation, and operational impact within agreed decision rights.

  • Communicate incident status, impact, uncertainty, actions underway, and the next update to technical and nontechnical stakeholders.

  • Manage cross-time-zone handoffs with explicit command ownership, current status, outstanding risks, pending decisions, and next actions.

  • Improve response readiness through exercises, playbooks, and post-incident reviews; track agreed corrective actions with their owners.

  • Partner with detection engineers to evaluate telemetry and detection quality, close incident-related visibility gaps, and prioritize practical response automation.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have personally led complex security incidents as incident commander or an equivalent response lead, with clear examples of decisions, delegation, escalation, and outcomes.

  • Make sound decisions with incomplete information and revise them as evidence changes, balancing containment urgency with operational impact.

  • Coordinate responders across teams and time zones, resolve conflicting priorities, and maintain clear ownership during handoffs.

  • Communicate calmly and precisely under pressure, including concise stakeholder updates and explicit statements of uncertainty.

  • Have the security and infrastructure fundamentals to challenge investigation findings and assess containment and recovery options.

  • Understand detection engineering, including telemetry coverage, detection logic, false positives and false negatives, and validation. Can query and interpret evidence to support response decisions.

  • Turn incident lessons into practical improvements to readiness, playbooks, detection coverage, and response tooling.

title: RTL Design Engineer – Interconnect & Network Datapath
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Hardware organization develops AI-native silicon and system-level solutions for the unique demands of advanced AI workloads. Building on efforts like Jalapeño, the team is developing future generations of AI-native silicon and tightly integrated systems to power the next generation of frontier models. By co-designing chips, systems, tools, and methodologies, the team helps deliver faster, more efficient, and production-ready hardware for OpenAI’s supercomputing platform.

About the Role

We are looking for a highly experienced, hands-on RTL engineer with deep packet-networking and interconnect expertise to own critical on- and off-chip communication components for our custom AI accelerator platform.

You will drive the microarchitecture and RTL implementation of scalable on-chip fabrics connecting high-bandwidth compute, memory, and I/O subsystems, as well as purpose-built off-chip interfaces and protocols that enable custom computing at scale. The ideal candidate has recently owned production RTL for networking or packet-switched datapaths such as Ethernet switches, NICs, SmartNICs, network accelerators, RDMA/RoCE systems, NoCs, or custom scale-up/scale-out fabrics.

This is a senior engineering role with broad technical ownership and substantial direct RTL work. You will drive designs from requirements and performance analysis through microarchitecture, SystemVerilog implementation, verification closure, physical design convergence, silicon bring-up, and production readiness. You will also plan and oversee the work of junior engineers and help develop productive engineering relationships with external partners.

In this role, you will:

  • Own the microarchitecture, RTL design, and delivery of major packet-based interconnect and networking components, including NoC fabrics, switches, routers, bridges, protocol adapters, arbiters, queues, schedulers, buffers, and traffic-management logic.

  • Design mechanisms for routing, arbitration, ordering, flow control, congestion management, quality of service, packet scheduling, buffering, and performance monitoring.

  • Develop on-chip and off-chip interfaces, protocol bridges, and custom networking protocols or protocol extensions for scale-up and scale-out systems.

  • Perform substantial direct microarchitecture, SystemVerilog coding, simulation, and debug work.

  • Collaborate with architecture and performance teams to analyze traffic patterns, identify bottlenecks, and optimize latency, bandwidth, fairness, and utilization under realistic workloads.

  • Work with verification teams to develop coverage plans, assertions, stress scenarios, and debug strategies for highly concurrent packet and fabric behavior.

  • Partner with physical design teams on floorplan-aware design, pipeline strategy, timing closure, power, area, and physical congestion.

  • Collaborate with firmware, software, validation, and post-silicon teams through bring-up and production readiness.

  • Drive third-party engagements involving networking, interface protocols, and silicon IP while maintaining design quality and execution accountability.

  • Provide technical leadership through architecture and design reviews, documentation, mentoring, and reusable RTL methodologies.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

  • Extensive industry experience with recent, hands-on ownership of complex networking, packet-processing, or packet-switched interconnect RTL.

  • Demonstrated networking expertise in one or more of the following: Ethernet switching, NIC/SmartNIC/DPU datapaths, network accelerators, RDMA/RoCE, InfiniBand, traffic management, or custom scale-up/scale-out transports.

  • Experience with relevant on-chip, chip-to-chip, or host interfaces such as AXI, CHI, CXL, PCIe, or Ethernet, alongside deeper networking or packet-datapath expertise.

  • Experience designing custom networking protocols, protocol extensions, or hardware datapaths for large-scale RDMA/RoCE, HPC, or AI systems.

  • Strong familiarity with RTL development and signoff flows, including lint, CDC/RDC, synthesis, formal verification, static timing analysis, power analysis, and design-for-test considerations.

  • Experience collaborating with architecture, verification, physical design, firmware, performance, and post-silicon teams to deliver complex silicon.

  • Strong judgment when balancing performance, power, area, schedule, verification risk, and physical implementation constraints.

  • The ability to provide technical direction, mentor engineers, and drive alignment while remaining actively involved in RTL design and debugging.

  • A passion for reducing complexity and improving engineering leverage through automation and pragmatic design.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience designing packet-switched interconnect or networking datapaths for AI accelerators, GPUs, CPUs, HPC systems, NICs/SmartNICs, switch ASICs, or large-scale datacenter silicon.

  • Experience addressing virtualization, isolation, RAS, telemetry, security, or memory-consistency requirements within complex networking or interconnect subsystems.

  • Experience with network or NoC performance modeling, traffic simulation, emulation, FPGA prototyping, or post-silicon traffic and performance analysis.

  • Experience leading architecture or RTL delivery for first-generation networking or interconnect IP in rapidly evolving silicon programs.

title: Training Performance Engineer
descriptionHtml:
About the Team
Training Runtime designs the core distributed machine-learning training runtime that powers everything from early research experiments to frontier-scale model runs. With a dual mandate to accelerate researchers and enable frontier scale, we’re building a unified, modular runtime that meets researchers where they are and moves with them up the scaling curve.

Our work focuses on three pillars: high-performance, asynchronous, zero-copy tensor and optimizer-state-aware data movement; performant, high-uptime, fault-tolerant training frameworks (training loop, state management, resilient checkpointing, deterministic orchestration, and observability); and distributed process management for long-lived, job-specific and user-provided processes.

We integrate proven large-scale capabilities into a composable, developer-facing runtime so teams can iterate quickly and run reliably at any scale, partnering closely with model-stack, research, and platform teams. Success for us is measured by raising both training throughput (how fast models train) and researcher throughput (how fast ideas become experiments and products).

About the Role
As a Training Performance Engineer, you’ll drive efficiency improvements across our distributed training stack. You’ll analyze large-scale training runs, identify utilization gaps, and design optimizations that push the boundaries of throughput and uptime. This role blends deep systems understanding with practical performance engineering — analyzing GPU kernel performance, collective communication throughput, investigating I/O bottlenecks, and sharding our models so we can train them at massive scale.

You’ll help ensure that our clusters are running at peak performance, enabling OpenAI to train larger, more capable models with the same compute budget.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of three days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

  • Profile end-to-end training runs to identify performance bottlenecks across compute, communication, and storage.

  • Optimize GPU utilization and throughput for large-scale distributed model training.

  • Collaborate with runtime and systems engineers to improve kernel efficiency, scheduling, and collective communication performance.

  • Implement model graph transforms to improve end to end throughput.

  • Build tooling to monitor and visualize MFU, throughput, and uptime across clusters.

  • Partner with researchers to ensure new model architectures scale efficiently during pre-training.

  • Contribute to infrastructure decisions that improve reliability and efficiency of large training jobs.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Love optimizing performance and digging into systems to understand how every layer interacts.

  • Have strong programming skills in Python and C++ (Rust or CUDA a plus).

  • Have experience running distributed training jobs on multi-GPU systems or HPC clusters.

  • Enjoy debugging complex distributed systems and measuring efficiency rigorously.

  • Have exposure to frameworks like PyTorch, JAX, or TensorFlow and an understanding of how large-scale training loops are built.

  • Are comfortable collaborating across teams and translating raw profiling data into practical engineering improvements.

Nice to have:

  • Familiarity with NCCL, MPI, or UCX communication libraries.

  • Experience with large-scale data loading and checkpointing systems.

  • Prior work on training runtime, distributed scheduling, or ML compiler optimization.

title: Applied AI Engineer, Enterprise - Healthcare Life Sciences (HLS)
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

Across industries, OpenAI’s Applied AI Engineering (AIE) team helps organizations turn frontier AI into safe, reliable production systems that deliver meaningful business outcomes. We work directly with customers’ engineering, product, security, and transformation teams to navigate complex architectures, data environments, governance requirements, and organization-wide change. We turn lessons from these deployments into better OpenAI products and reusable patterns that help customers move faster.

About the Role

As an Enterprise AIE, you will serve as a technical partner to leading organizations within the Healthcare and Life Sciences segment (HLS), helping them turn ambitious AI use cases into durable production systems and adoption at scale. You will combine deep technical judgment with hands-on engineering to provide technical leadership on complex customer deployments. You will write and debug code, build evaluation systems, resolve complex integrations, and guide decisions about model behavior, reliability, latency, cost, safety, security, governance, and operational readiness. You will work across clinical, operational, administrative and research workflows, translating security, privacy and governance requirements into practical deployment decisions. Success is measured by durable production systems, sustained adoption, and meaningful business impact. Your deployment experience will also directly influence how OpenAI’s products evolve.

This role may be based in one of our offices in New York City or San Francisco, or it may be performed remotely. Office-based employees follow a hybrid work model with three days per week in the office. We offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In This Role, You Will

  • Work hands-on in code to design, build, evaluate, and deploy AI systems from prototype to reliable production and scaled adoption that solve important customer problems and deliver measurable business outcomes.

  • Partner with enterprise customers to identify high-value opportunities and translate them into technical architectures, implementation plans, evaluation strategies, and success criteria.

  • Make sound technical decisions across model selection, agent and tool design, retrieval, context design, data pipelines, evaluation, reliability, observability, latency, cost, safety, security, and governance.

  • Diagnose complex implementation challenges, reproduce failures, test hypotheses, and drive blockers to resolution.

  • Partner closely with customers’ engineering teams and OpenAI’s Product, Research, Engineering, Security, and Go-to-Market teams to turn deployment experience into actionable product feedback.

  • Partner with customer security, privacy, clinical and business teams to design responsible AI deployments, including data handling, access controls, evaluation, human oversight and monitoring.

  • Create reusable architectures, tooling, playbooks, and technical guidance that accelerate future enterprise deployments.

You Might Thrive in This Role If You

  • Have personally designed, built, and shipped AI or machine-learning systems in enterprise environments, taking them from prototype to production and making substantial contributions through coding, architecture, evaluation, debugging, or production engineering. Relevant backgrounds may include applied AI or ML engineering, forward-deployed engineering, software engineering, customer engineering, solutions architecture, or technical consulting.

  • Are highly proficient in Python and comfortable working end to end across model APIs, agent and tool development, retrieval and data pipelines, evaluation, observability, integrations, and production operations. Experience with JavaScript, TypeScript, or another relevant language is valuable.

descriptionHtml:

OpenAI builds powerful AI systems like ChatGPT, the OpenAI API, and enterprise products that serve millions of users across the globe. As we scale, securing our infrastructure, protecting sensitive data, supporting employees’ velocity, and meeting global compliance standards are essential to our success and societal impact.

Security at OpenAI is a cross-cutting organization that includes Security, Privacy, IT, GRC, Corporate Security, and other teams. Program Managers play a critical role in aligning teams and delivering execution at scale.

You will also apply what you build to other priorities that span Security teams.
