title: Engineering Manager, Guardian
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The Guardian team builds practical safety and oversight systems for increasingly capable AI agents. Our goal is to make it possible for agents to take on longer-running, higher-autonomy work while preserving meaningful safeguards, respecting user intent, and intervening when actions could cause serious or difficult-to-reverse harm.

Auto-review is an early example of this work. When an agent reaches a permission boundary, a separate model evaluates the proposed action in context and determines whether it should proceed. The team is now extending this foundation into more capable oversight systems that account for richer user context, support a broader range of agent experiences, and integrate across OpenAI products.

Guardian sits at the intersection of engineering, alignment research, product, infrastructure, and security. The team already has a strong engineering foundation in London and will continue to grow there as a concentrated, highly collaborative group.

About the Role

We are looking for an Engineering Manager to lead and grow the Guardian team in London. You will own the engineering strategy and execution for production systems that evaluate agent behavior, identify risk, and take appropriate action without creating unnecessary friction for users.

This is a builder-manager role with substantial technical depth. You will set direction, develop engineers, and create the operating cadence for a high-performing team, while remaining close enough to the work to shape architecture, review designs, debug difficult problems, and write code when it is the highest-leverage way to help the team move forward.

The role is highly visible and cross-functional. You will work closely with alignment researchers to translate emerging research into dependable systems, and with product teams to make agent safety a foundational capability across OpenAI.

This role is based in our London office.

In this role, you will

  • Lead, hire, and develop a London-based team of engineers working across agent safety, backend systems, applied AI, and product infrastructure.

  • Set the technical roadmap for Auto-review and the broader Guardian platform, balancing safety, product utility, latency, and operational reliability.

  • Build production systems that evaluate agent actions in real time, detect potentially harmful behavior, and support safe recovery or escalation paths.

  • Improve how oversight systems understand user intent, environmental context, permissions, and relevant personalization signals while protecting privacy and avoiding unnecessary friction.

  • Partner closely with alignment researchers to turn prototypes, evaluations, and new monitoring techniques into scalable product capabilities.

  • Work across Product, Security, Infrastructure, and other engineering teams to integrate Guardian capabilities into agent experiences throughout OpenAI.

  • Establish rigorous evaluation and operational practices, including adversarial testing, failure analysis, monitoring, and metrics for safety performance, false positives, latency, and user impact.


You might thrive in this role if you

  • Have significant experience leading engineering teams that shipped complex, high-stakes production systems end to end.

  • Have built with AI agents or large language models in a core product, startup, or technically serious independent project, and understand the unique challenges of agentic systems.

  • Bring strong product-engineering judgment and can navigate tradeoffs across safety, usability, speed, and reliability.

  • Can partner effectively with research teams, translate open-ended findings into engineering plans, and communicate clearly across technical disciplines.

title: Software Engineer, CI/CD & ML Infrastructure
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Hardware organization develops AI-native silicon and system-level solutions for the unique demands of advanced AI workloads. Building on efforts like Jalapeño, the team is developing future generations of AI-native silicon and tightly integrated systems to power the next generation of frontier models. By co-designing chips, systems, tools, and methodologies, the team helps deliver faster, more efficient, and production-ready hardware for OpenAI’s supercomputing platform.

About the Role

You will define and build the CI/CD systems that qualify frontier models and the software stack running on OpenAI’s custom AI accelerators. Your work will make correctness, performance, and stability measurable on every change, from individual commits through production releases.

This role spans model workloads, accelerator software, systems infrastructure, and developer productivity. You will establish scalable CI/CD, GitOps, and monorepo practices; design trustworthy regression and benchmarking pipelines; and partner with model, compiler, kernel, runtime, firmware, and hardware teams to shorten feedback loops without compromising production readiness.

In this role, you will:

  • Define the model CI strategy for frontier models running on OpenAI custom silicon and integrated accelerator systems.

  • Build production CI/CD pipelines for functional regression, performance benchmarking, software stability, and release qualification.

  • Design representative test matrices across models, configurations, hardware generations, software components, and deployment environments.

  • Create reliable performance baselines, regression detection, bisect and triage workflows, and clear ownership for failures.

  • Establish GitOps practices for reproducible configuration, promotion, rollback, auditability, and environment consistency.

  • Shape monorepo architecture, dependency management, build and test boundaries, change validation, and developer workflows at scale.

  • Develop scalable orchestration, artifact management, caching, scheduling, observability, and capacity controls for accelerator-backed CI.

  • Partner with model, compiler, kernel, runtime, firmware, validation, and hardware teams to translate release risks into automated gates.

  • Improve CI reliability, speed, debuggability, and cost efficiency while maintaining high confidence in production software.

You might thrive in this role if:

title: Safety Transparency Editor, Safety Systems
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

Safety Systems works to ensure OpenAI’s most capable models can be developed and deployed responsibly. Our work spans evaluations, safeguards, red teaming, deployment decisions, and the systems that help OpenAI understand and reduce risk as models become more capable and widely used.

Within Safety Systems, the Trustworthy AI team is growing its safety transparency function: a practice focused on helping external audiences understand OpenAI’s technical safety work with greater clarity, rigor, and continuity. We create and improve the public artifacts that explain how our systems are evaluated for safety, what safeguards we build, what decisions we make, and where uncertainty remains.

This work includes system cards, the Deployment Safety Hub, safety-related blogs, public governance documents, and other outputs that communicate technical safety topics to external audiences. It also includes building new ways to make technical safety information easier to understand, navigate, and use—including AI-assisted workflows, data visualizations, and interactive tools that make complex technical work more legible over time.


About the Role

We are looking for a Safety Transparency Editor to own the editorial quality of key safety transparency artifacts and systems.

This is a hands-on role for someone who can write crystal-clear, pitch-perfect explanations of the hardest and highest-stakes technical safety topics that OpenAI tackles, and who can lean into AI to build systems that help the broader organization do this work better.

Your core responsibility is to shape and execute how our technical safety work is externally communicated: identifying the narrative thread, exercising judgment about which details matter, determining where additional context, explanation, or supporting evidence is needed, translating complexity without sacrificing precision, and helping external audiences understand both the safety measures we’ve taken and the uncertainties that remain. To do this work effectively, you will need to be comfortable educating yourself, using AI tools and existing internal evidence, about the nuances of technical safety work taking place across OpenAI.

You will serve as the editorial driver behind system cards and related transparency materials, partnering closely with Safety Programs, researchers, evaluators, red-teamers, policy experts, legal partners, product marketing and communications teams, and other launch stakeholders. You will transform complex technical safety topics into public-facing artifacts that are rigorous, accessible, and faithful to the underlying substance.

You’ll also be expected to use AI deeply in your own practice—not simply as a learning and drafting tool, but as a means of rethinking how this work gets done. You should instinctively look for opportunities to build workflows, automate repetitive tasks, improve consistency, and create systems that enable the organization to produce high-quality transparency artifacts at scale and speed.

This role demands deep ownership and accountability. The ideal candidate is equally at home refining a tricky explanation of a nuanced technical point, and investing in building systems that make the next ten explanations easier to produce.

This role is ideal for someone who combines the judgment of an exceptional editor with the mindset of a builder. You should be comfortable using your voice and judgment while approaching the work with humility, intellectual honesty, and a deep respect for technical nuance.

In This Role, You Will

Serve as the narrative DRI for system cards and related transparency artifacts from initiation through publication.

Partner with the Safety Programs team, researchers, evaluators, red-teamers, policy experts, legal teams, communications partners, and launch teams to translate technical findings into public-facing materials.

Write clear, precise explanations of highly technical safety topics for external audiences without sacrificing rigor or nuance.

Shape the editorial structure and narrative arc of transparency artifacts, ensuring they accurately communicate what OpenAI has done, why it matters, and where uncertainty remains.

Exercise strong editorial judgment to determine what context is necessary, what caveats should be highlighted, and where additional explanation or supporting evidence may be needed to strengthen public understanding.

Improve repeatable editorial processes, templates, and publication workflows.

Use AI tools to accelerate drafting, synthesize source materials, identify precedents, prepare reviewer packets, and improve consistency across artifacts.

Build systems and workflows that make transparency efforts faster, more scalable, and more effective over time.

Support blogs, governance documents, technical explainers, and other technical safety communications when needed.

Help evolve the Deployment Safety Hub and related transparency surfaces over time.


Example Projects

Drive the narrative, framing, and technical writing and editing for a system card supporting a major model launch.

Translate novel evaluation methodologies, preparedness frameworks, and mitigation approaches into explanations accessible to policymakers, journalists, researchers, and external experts.

Build an AI-assisted workflow that improves consistency, quality, and efficiency of our safety transparency practice.

Help shape the evolution of the Deployment Safety Hub as a trusted destination for understanding OpenAI’s technical safety work.


You Might Thrive in This Role If You

Are an exceptional writer and editor who can make highly technical topics understandable without sacrificing precision.

Have strong editorial judgment and know how to identify the narrative thread in complex, ambiguous material, surfacing what details matter, what context is needed, and how to communicate uncertainty responsibly.

Have strong execution instincts and enjoy owning complex projects from start to finish.

Can synthesize diverse inputs into structured, publication-ready artifacts.

Can earn trust and work in close partnership with technical experts to make their work accessible without oversimplifying it.

Are deeply AI-native in how you work, and instinctively look for opportunities to automate, systematize, and improve editorial processes.

Care deeply about rigor, intellectual honesty, and earning trust through accuracy.

Have the confidence to use your voice and judgment while remaining humble, evidence-driven, and open to feedback.

Enjoy learning unfamiliar technical domains quickly and developing fluency in frontier AI safety concepts.

title: Mechanical Design Engineer, Motor Design & Prototyping
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

Our Robotics team is focused on unlocking general-purpose robotics and pushing towards AGI-level intelligence in dynamic, real-world settings. Working across the entire model stack, we integrate cutting-edge hardware and software to explore a broad range of robotic form factors. We strive to seamlessly blend high-level AI capabilities with the constraints of physical systems to improve peoples’ lives.

About the Role

We are seeking a Mechanical Design Engineer to lead the development of motor mechanical designs and prototype hardware for advanced robotic systems. You will own stator and rotor mechanical development from early concepts and detailed design through hands-on builds and prototype validation, partnering closely with electromagnetic, electrical, test, and manufacturing teams.

This role focuses on the design, integration, and validation of motor components and prototype processes, including laminations, stack assemblies, bobbins, winding interfaces, and fixtures. You will help drive motor development from initial design through repeatable low-volume builds while establishing the tooling, work instructions, and validation practices needed for future robotic platforms.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA, and requires in-person presence 4 days a week.

In this role, you will

  • Own stator and rotor mechanical designs and released CAD and drawings, including geometry, interfaces, fits, tolerances, retention, assembly access, and mechanical validation.

  • Develop laminations, stack assembly methods, bobbins, and winding interfaces that control alignment, insulation, conductor placement, and end-turn packaging.

  • Design, fabricate, and debug fixtures for winding, stacking, assembly, alignment, and inspection.

  • Build and troubleshoot prototypes. Use measurements, defects, rework, and assembly effort to improve designs and processes.

  • Establish low-volume prototype production with equipment, build sequences, work instructions, revision control, traceability, and acceptance checks that let technicians reproduce successful builds.

  • Test new manufacturing methods and winding approaches, balancing performance, repeatability, and practical implementation.

  • Work with electromagnetic, electrical, manufacturing, and test engineers to resolve tradeoffs between motor performance, packaging, buildability, and validation.

You might thrive in this role if you

  • Move comfortably between CAD, the shop, measurements, and hands-on builds, and take ownership of the physical result.

  • Understand how tolerances, insulation, tool access, and assembly sequence affect whether a motor can be built and used reliably.

  • Diagnose failed builds through evidence and focused experiments, then carry the fix into the next iteration.

title: Software Engineer, Agent Identity
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The Agent Identity team builds the foundational identity infrastructure that enables AI agents to securely act on behalf of users and organizations. We develop the systems that allow agents to establish their identity, demonstrate whose authority they are operating under, and securely access resources across applications and environments.

Our team owns agent identity and delegation, authentication and authorization, credential lifecycle management, revocation, and integrations with external platforms. We also build Sign in with ChatGPT, enabling OpenAI to serve as an identity provider across a growing ecosystem of applications.

As AI agents become increasingly autonomous, our work is foundational to how users, organizations, and developers establish trust in agentic systems.

About the Role

We are looking for experienced software engineers to design and build the identity infrastructure powering the next generation of AI agents across OpenAI’s products, including ChatGPT and Codex.

You will tackle complex, largely unsolved engineering challenges at the intersection of identity, security, distributed systems, and agent infrastructure. You’ll help define how agents authenticate across environments, how users securely delegate authority to agents, and how agents interact with external applications and services.

This is an opportunity to shape foundational technical primitives at OpenAI while helping influence how the broader industry approaches identity in an increasingly agent-driven world.

In this role, you will:

  • Design and build foundational agent identity primitives, including agent authentication, delegated authorization, and credential lifecycle management.

  • Develop secure mechanisms that enable agents to act on behalf of users and organizations across internal and external systems.

  • Architect authentication and authorization flows for connectors, third-party applications, and cloud-based agent execution environments.

  • Build and evolve Sign in with ChatGPT, enabling secure identity federation and interoperability across the broader application ecosystem.

  • Design highly scalable, reliable, and secure distributed systems that support credential issuance, rotation, revocation, and access enforcement.

  • Partner closely with engineering, product, security, and external platform teams to solve emerging identity challenges and help shape industry standards.

  • Drive technical direction and own complex initiatives from initial architecture through production deployment.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have experience designing, building, and operating large-scale distributed systems or business-critical backend infrastructure.

  • Have deep technical experience in identity and access management, workload identity, identity providers, authentication, authorization, or credential lifecycle management.

  • Alternatively, have experience building cloud-based AI agents, agent execution environments, browser-based automation, or connector infrastructure, with firsthand exposure to identity and authentication challenges.

  • Have familiarity with identity and authorization protocols such as OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect, or related emerging standards.

  • Bring a security-first mindset and proactively consider trust boundaries, failure modes, and potential abuse when designing systems.

  • Thrive in ambiguous problem spaces where established technical patterns may not yet exist, and enjoy defining solutions from first principles.

  • Have a track record of driving complex technical initiatives, influencing architectural decisions, and collaborating effectively across engineering teams.

  • Are excited about defining how identity, trust, and delegated authority will work in a world where AI agents increasingly act on our behalf.

title: Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE), Life Sciences - NYC
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Forward Deployed Engineering team partners with global pharma and biotech, CROs, and research institutions to deploy existing expertise across the R&D value chain to help customers design and ship production-grade AI systems. We operate at the intersection of customer delivery and core platform development, converting early deployments into repeatable system standards and evaluation practices that scale across regulated environments.

About the Role

We are hiring a Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) to push the frontier on what is possible today across drug discovery (e.g., target identification, molecular design, pre-clinical) and development (e.g., trial design, trial ops, biostats) by leading end-to-end deployments of our models inside life sciences organizations and research institutions. You will work with customers who are deep experts in their scientific or operational domains, translating real-world data, infrastructure, and constraints into production systems.

You will measure success through production adoption, measurable workflow impact, and eval-driven feedback loops, including evaluation benchmarks and acceptance criteria, that inform product and model roadmaps. You’ll work closely with our Product, Research, Partnerships, GRC, Security, and GTM to deliver in regulated contexts, including inspection readiness with audit trails and traceable evidence.

This role is based in New York. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week. We offer relocation assistance. Travel up to 50% is required.

In this role, you will:

  • Design and ship production systems around models, owning integrations, data provenance, reliability, and on-call readiness across research, clinical, and operational workflows.

  • Lead discovery and scoping from pre-sales through post-sales, translating ambiguous workflow needs into hypothesis-driven problem framing, system requirements, and an execution plan with measurable endpoints.

  • Define and enforce launch criteria for regulated contexts, including validation evidence, audit readiness, outcome metrics, and drive delivery until we demonstrate sustained production impact.

  • Build in sensitive scientific data environments where auditability, validation, and access controls shape architecture, operating procedures, and failure handling.

  • Run evaluation loops that measure model and system quality against workflow-specific scientific benchmarks and use results to drive model and product changes.

  • Distill deployment learnings into hardened primitives, reference architectures, validation templates, and benchmark harnesses that scale across regulated life sciences environments.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Bring 5+ years of software/ML engineering or technical deployment experience with customer-facing ownership in biotech, pharma, clinical research, or scientific software; PhD, MS, or equivalent applied experience in a life sciences relevant field encouraged.

  • Have owned customer GenAI deployments end-to-end from scoping through production adoption, and improved them through evaluation design, error analysis, and iterative evidence generation that tightens acceptance criteria over time.

  • Have delivered AI systems in trial design, regulatory writing, or scientific operations where validation strategy, auditability, compliance constraints, and reviewer expectations shaped system design and rollout.

  • Communicate clearly across scientific, clinical, model research, technical, and executive audiences, translating technical tradeoffs into decision quality, risk posture, and measurable outcomes with credibility.

title: Head of Community, EMEA
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI’s mission is to ensure that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity.

The Community team focuses on finding exceptional power users of our tools and turning real usage into stories and signals that shape both product direction and how the world understands OpenAI. We do that by learning directly from users, then working together to package insights and use cases into formats that can travel: playbooks, webpages, launch assets, event series, and clear guidance on how people actually use our tools.

About the Role

The Head of Community, EMEA,will lead OpenAI’s community presence across the region and be responsible for setting and evolving an evidence-based Community strategy in markets, including hiring local community leads and managers .

The role is responsible for how we create trusted relationships with power users and translate those relationships into participation, insight, enablement, and stories across the region. They will partner with senior leadership to recommend where Community can have the greatest impact across EMEA, laddering up to company and country level priorities.

Immediately, they will oversee our Student Collective motion in EMEA markets, including working with our global team, global agency and hiring Student Community Managers and coordinators in markets. They will also shape how we roll out additional community work with SMBs and Pro subscribers in close collaboration with the global program leads.

We’re looking for an experienced community leader who has held senior roles at multiple companies, including those where community is central to how people learn, build, create, or share their work.

They understand how to combine thoughtful relationships with programs that can reach many more people. They are comfortable building the first relationships themselves, identifying what makes them valuable, and developing a team that can sustain that quality as the work grows.

They bring strong judgement about which communities and fandoms to invest in, how global programs should adapt to local needs, and how community learning can inform decisions across OpenAI.

In this role, you will:

Build the broader EMEA Community strategy:

  • Map the EMEA community landscape and develop a point of view on which user communities OpenAI should know, support and learn from.

  • Build high-trust direct relationships with power users across relevant segments, and help scale that relationship building motion across EMEA where strategically justified.

  • Define a clear expansion logic: which communities and fandoms to explore, why they matter, what Community can uniquely contribute and what resourcing they require.

  • Develop country and regional priorities together with country leads, combining local community insights, market context, and company goals.

  • Create repeatable playbooks for launching, learning from and scaling community programs across EMEA without losing local relevance.

Lead regional community programs:

  • Partner with country leads and local Community teams to develop market priorities and programs, drawing on local user insights and cultural context while maintaining accountability for regional outcomes.

  • Work with global program leads and country leads to adapt global programs, develop initiatives originating in markets, and share successful approaches across EMEA, with clear expectations for member experience, participation, and learning.

  • Oversee the Student Collective across EMEA, working with the agency partner and hiring and supporting local Student Community Managers and Coordinators in markets.

  • Shape and deliver SMB and Pro subscriber programs with global and country leads, including targeted engagement with knowledge worker communities and fandoms where there is a clear opportunity.

Turn relationships into participation, insights, and stories:

  • Source and curate compelling use cases and stories, spotlight community members, and equip them to share their knowledge with wider audiences, helping more people discover practical ways to use AI

  • Synthesise patterns by market, community, segment and use case; distinguish isolated anecdotes from signals worth acting on.

  • Publish regular updates and recaps that highlight progress, insights, risks and opportunities and clear recommendations.

  • Work cross-functionally to route relevant learnings into product, research, brand and product marketing, education, communications,and global affair teams so that these stories and insights can benefit millions more around the world.

Operate and scale the function:

  • Hire, support, and develop regional and market teams needed to grow EMEA Community work, maintaining the quality of user relationships as programs scale.

  • Work with our global team to build the systems, dashboards, cadences, xfn partners, templates and decision making processes needed to run EMEA Community work well.

  • Coordinate with internal and external stakeholders to ensure alignment, clear ownership and follow-through.

  • Manage multiple workstreams across markets and communities while keeping priorities clear and execution moving.

  • Identify where additional local capacity, agency support, translation or specialist expertise is needed.

  • Represent OpenAI credibly with community members, campus partners and regional ecosystem stakeholders.

What success looks like:

  • Strong regional and market community team delivering effective community programs, including the Student Collective and emerging SMB and Pro subscriber initiatives. Clear recommendations on which communities and programs to scale, adapt, pause, or invest in, developed with country leads.

  • A clear, evidence-based view of which EMEA communities and markets matter most now and next. A practical regional operating model that can scale across markets while preserving local relevance.

  • High-trust user relationships that lead to robust participation, useful insights, and breakthrough stories, helping OpenAI improve product, marketing, education, and communications decisions while growing advocates in the region.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have 10+ years of experience building, leading or scaling communities, user programmes or ecosystem initiatives across EMEA.

  • Have experience hiring and developing community teams, managing contractors and agencies, and leading cross-functional workstreams across markets with clear priorities and strong follow-through.

  • Are an excellent executor who can operate in ambiguous, fast-moving environments.

  • Bring strong qualitative judgement and can build trust, identify patterns and turn community signals into clear recommendations.

  • Have excellent written and verbal communication skills and can influence stakeholders without direct authority.

  • Are experienced and comfortable working across markets, cultures and time zones, and willing to travel for community activations and relationship-building.

  • Have a strong interest in AI and practical familiarity with how people use ChatGPT or other AI tools.

Preferred qualifications:

  1. Experience with student, campus, youth, creator, developer, professional, or other power-user communities.

  2. Strong network across relevant EMEA communities, institutions, or ecosystem partners.

  3. Experience translating community insight into stories, playbooks, launches, programs, or product recommendations.

  4. Fluency in one or more additional EMEA languages.

title: Deployment Lead, FDE - SF
descriptionHtml:
About the team

OpenAI’s Forward Deployed Engineering (FDE) team partners with customers to turn research breakthroughs into production systems. We operate at the intersection of customer delivery and core platform development.

About the Role

As a Deployment Lead, you’ll lead some of OpenAI’s most strategic AI engagements from the first executive conversation through production and adoption. You’ll work with executive sponsors to understand what they want to change, spend time with the people who do the work today, and partner with engineers to test what’s feasible. Alongside the account director, you’ll turn what you learn into a case for investment and a deployment plan both teams can commit to.

You will own delivery end-to-end: embedding with customers to map workflows and success criteria, ensuring components ship on time, and leading readiness and change management for adoption. You’ll track progress, manage dependencies, make sequencing decisions, and drive 0→1 prototypes through MVP and scale. You will also share field insights with Product and Research to guide roadmap and priorities.

Success will be measured first and foremost by impact - deployments that deliver measurable value against customer goals, drive adoption, and become critical to their workflows. Additional measures of success include delivery reliability (milestones hit), operating leverage (patterns reused across deployments), judgment under pressure, and product impact (field signal that shifts roadmaps).

This is a high-trust, high-autonomy role. Success requires deep technical project management expertise, extreme ownership of outcomes, and an ability to immerse in customer workflows and partner with customer teams to solve complex engineering problems at pace.

This role is based in New York City or San Francisco. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week. We offer relocation assistance. Travel between 25-50% is required.

In this role, you will:

  • Scope and win strategic customer engagements partnering with the account director. Work with customer teams and engineers to prioritize what to build and map the path to production. Turn those choices into a phased proposal defining each side’s commitments, what phase one must prove, and when to expand.

  • Own value cases and ROI. Set impact hypotheses, baselines, and KPIs; run pre/post deployment measurement and report to exec sponsors.

  • Own the technical delivery plan for multiple work streams. Translate business objectives into a roadmap with milestones, dependencies, and acceptance criteria. Run day-to-day engineering execution and keep progress unblocked.

  • Shape account strategy with the account director. Build relationships with customer executives from scoping through adoption. Connect deployment results to business priorities, resolve trade-offs, and agree on where to invest next.

  • Embed with customer teams to land production deployments and drive adoption. Map workflows, shape tools/integrations, and translate requirements into a delivery plan. Lead onboarding, adoption, and change management.

  • Codify solution patterns and evals. Extract reusable patterns and package field signals to improve product and models.

  • Partner with Product and Research so platform components and research work streams land in time to support deployment goals.


You’ll thrive in this role if you:

  • Bring 7+ years of customer‑facing technical delivery leadership.

  • Track record of successfully leading large, complex, high-stakes customer engagements where customer outcomes depended on tight coordination and fast decision making, ideally involving AI.

  • You’ve helped win or expand a complex technology engagement. You’ve shaped the scope with engineers, influenced what the customer chose to fund, and led delivery against the commitments you helped make.

  • You’re a translator with executive presence. You make complex technical trade-offs legible to business leaders and convert strategy into day-to-day technical execution.

  • You have shipped AI/LLM systems, have strong technical fluency and understand production pitfalls.

  • You are able to step back from execution detail, recognize broader trends across deployments, and connect customer needs to scalable, reusable solutions.

  • Excel in high ambiguity environments where you help build the function.

  • Have expertise in at least one major sector (e.g., healthcare, life sciences, energy, financial services, semiconductors, legal) to elevate solution framing and credibility.

OpenAI's Legal team plays a crucial role in furthering OpenAI's mission by tackling innovative, fundamental legal issues in AI. If you're passionate about doing significant and unique work as a technology lawyer, this team is for you. The team comprises professionals from diverse fields, including technology, AI, privacy, IP, corporate, employment, tax law, regulatory, and litigation.

As a member of our Product Counsel team, you will advise on a broad range of issues arising from hardware products and technologies, with a focus on software that power them. You’ll work closely with software engineering, product, design, and business teams from development through launch and ongoing support. About the Team

OpenAI’s Industrial Compute team is responsible for building and scaling large-scale compute capacity across first-party data centers, strategic partners, and industrial infrastructure environments. We focus on converting power, land, hardware, and operational execution into reliable compute capacity that can support frontier AI training and inference workloads.

This team operates at the intersection of infrastructure delivery, hardware systems, utilities, supply chain, and capacity strategy—ensuring OpenAI can scale compute faster than traditional models allow.

We are seeking a GPT Infrastructure Lead to drive the end-to-end conversion of industrial-scale infrastructure investments into usable token capacity for OpenAI workloads.

In this role, you will own execution across complex compute programs where raw infrastructure capacity must be transformed into operational GPU throughput. You will coordinate across data center delivery, power, networking, hardware deployment, workload enablement, finance, and external partners to ensure capacity becomes productive tokens as quickly and efficiently as possible.

descriptionHtml:

AI will change how the world works. Human connection will shape what it becomes. OpenAI’s Events and Experiences team, part of Business Marketing, carries the critical responsibility of bringing people together around OpenAI’s mission – building artificial general intelligence that benefits all of humanity. title: Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE), Cyber - SF
descriptionHtml:
About the team

OpenAI’s Forward Deployed Engineering team builds with customers to bring frontier AI into production. Our Cyber FDEs partner with the security and engineering teams that defend globally critical systems, from enterprise software to the core infrastructure it runs on. Cyber FDEs work closely with our Product, Research, and Go-to-Market teams to adapt our products and models to what customers need to defend their systems.

About the role

You’ll build systems that give defenders an advantage at a scale few engineering teams encounter. You might help an enterprise identify, test, and deploy patches across hundreds of thousands of code repositories, or help a security team analyze petabytes of logs for signs of malicious agents or coordinated attacks. Across these deployments, you’ll build tools that customer engineers can trust to support consequential security decisions.

You’ll work directly with customer security teams, from CISOs to frontline analysts. As AI changes how attackers operate, you’ll help these teams determine where their defenses need to evolve, prioritize what to build, and validate solutions with the engineers who will operate them. Alongside OpenAI’s account teams, you’ll translate security priorities into deployed systems that help defenders cover more ground.

You’ll also help shape what OpenAI builds next. When you identify a gap between what defenders need and what today’s models or products can do, you’ll partner with Research and Product to define, build, and test capabilities that address it.

This role is based in San Francisco. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week. We offer relocation assistance. Travel up to 50% is required.

In this role you will:

  • Partner with customer security leaders and OpenAI’s Go-to-Market team to scope engagements, establish responsibilities, and define measurable success criteria.

  • Lead technical design and implementation alongside customer engineers. Integrate agents into security workflows, establish access boundaries, and determine which actions require human review.

  • Build evaluations grounded in the decisions defenders make. For a patching agent, test whether a fix blocks a known exploit while preserving expected application behavior. For a detection system, replay historical attacks alongside normal traffic to measure detection speed and false-positive rates.

  • Guide production rollout with the engineers who will operate the system. Provide the observability and controls they need to understand system behavior, intervene when necessary, and expand adoption with confidence.

  • Translate successful approaches across deployments into reusable tools and engineering practices that other defenders can adopt.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • 5+ years of software engineering experience, including building and shipping production software.

  • Experience protecting production systems through work in security engineering, infrastructure, SRE, DevOps, or product engineering.

  • Experience building and evaluating AI agents for software engineering workflows.

  • Experience with CI/CD pipelines and practices that maintain code quality, reliability, and security.

  • Ability to navigate unfamiliar codebases and contribute maintainable, production-quality changes.

  • Ability to communicate technical concepts and trade-offs to engineering teams and senior security stakeholders.

Additional experience

Cybersecurity spans many disciplines, and while we’re primarily looking for strong engineering generalists, we’d love to hear about deeper experience in any of the following areas:

  • Security curiosity and experimentation: You read CVE write-ups because you want to understand how things break. You may have built an agent honeypot to test a hypothesis—or prove a point—and enjoy turning a security question into a hands-on experiment.

  • Security community engagement: You enjoy exchanging ideas with defenders, whether that’s discussing security strategy with a CISO at Black Hat or comparing technical approaches with frontline practitioners.

  • Application security: You’ve written CodeQL queries or Semgrep rules, built fuzzing harnesses, or discovered and responsibly disclosed vulnerabilities.

  • Automated remediation: CI/CD is your happy place. You’ve built tooling that turns security findings into tested patches, dependency upgrades, or configuration changes across large codebases.

  • Detection engineering: You’ve written and deployed detections using Sigma, YARA, Splunk, or KQL and tested them against attacker behavior.

  • Cloud and identity security: You’ve designed cloud IAM architectures and investigated abuse of workload identities, role hierarchies, or cross-account trust.

  • Security research: You’ve reverse-engineered malware, developed exploit reproductions, or contributed to vulnerability research.

  • Agent security: You’ve tested agents for prompt injection, tool misuse, or credential exposure and built defenses against them.

You are a hands-on leader who can coach through a complex customer conversation, build an actionable plan from data, and bring clarity and focus in a fast-changing environment. You balance near-term results with long-term customer partnerships and make thoughtful decisions that protect user trust.

title: PCBA Manufacturing Engineer
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI's Industrial Compute organization is building the world's most advanced AI infrastructure ecosystem. We work closely with hardware design teams, manufacturing partners, suppliers, and data center operations to deliver the compute platforms that power frontier AI.

The Manufacturing Engineering team ensures our hardware can be built, tested, deployed, and supported at hyperscale. We bridge Hardware Engineering, Quality, Supply Chain, Contract Manufacturers, and Hardware Operations to continuously improve manufacturing performance throughout the product lifecycle.

As our fleet grows globally, sustaining manufacturing engineering becomes increasingly important to maintain product quality, improve manufacturability, and rapidly resolve production issues.

About the Role

We are seeking a PCBA Manufacturing Engineer (Sustaining) to support production and continuous improvement of printed circuit board assemblies (PCBAs) used throughout Industrial Compute hardware platforms.

This role focuses on sustaining engineering after product launch. You'll partner closely with Hardware Design, Quality, Manufacturing, Test Engineering, Supply Chain, and our contract manufacturers to resolve production issues, improve manufacturing yield, reduce failures, implement engineering changes, and ensure stable high-volume manufacturing.

The ideal candidate has experience supporting complex server, networking, accelerator, storage, or high-performance electronics manufacturing environments.

Key Responsibilities

  • Own sustaining manufacturing engineering for PCBA production across multiple hardware platforms.

  • Drive root cause investigations for manufacturing defects, field failures, and production escapes.

  • Partner with Hardware Design Engineers to improve manufacturability (DFM/DFA/DFT).

  • Support engineering change orders (ECOs) and manufacturing change implementation.

  • Work directly with contract manufacturers to improve production yield, cycle time, and quality.

  • Analyze manufacturing data to identify recurring process issues and improvement opportunities.

  • Develop corrective and preventive actions (CAPA) for manufacturing and supplier quality issues.

  • Support failure analysis activities including electrical, functional, and process investigations.

  • Improve manufacturing documentation, work instructions, assembly processes, and test procedures.

  • Collaborate with Test Engineering to improve production test coverage and manufacturing diagnostics.

  • Support supplier qualification, process validation, and manufacturing readiness for design revisions.

  • Travel to manufacturing partners as needed to support production and issue resolution.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, or related field.

  • 5+ years supporting high-volume PCBA manufacturing.

  • Experience with SMT manufacturing, PCB fabrication, and electronic assembly processes.

  • Strong understanding of manufacturing process control, yield improvement, and statistical analysis.

  • Experience performing root cause analysis using methodologies such as 8D, 5 Why, Fishbone, or FMEA.

  • Experience working with contract manufacturers and global supply chains.

  • Ability to interpret schematics, BOMs, assembly drawings, and manufacturing documentation.

  • Excellent cross-functional communication and project management skills.

Preferred Skills

  • Experience with server, accelerator, networking, storage, or AI hardware platforms.

  • Familiarity with ICT, Flying Probe, Boundary Scan, Functional Test, and System-Level Test.

  • Experience supporting high-speed PCBAs involving GPUs, CPUs, memory, PCIe, Ethernet, or high-speed interconnects.

  • Knowledge of IPC standards (IPC-A-610, IPC-6012, IPC-7711/7721).

  • Experience with manufacturing execution systems (MES), PLM systems, and engineering change management.

  • Enjoy solving complex manufacturing problems using data and structured root cause analysis.

  • Like working directly with manufacturing partners and factory teams.

  • Can bridge hardware design and manufacturing execution.

  • Have strong troubleshooting skills across electronics, assembly processes, and production testing.

  • Enjoy continuous improvement and process optimization.

  • Are comfortable balancing technical depth with fast operational execution.

descriptionHtml:
About the Team

Frontier AI is changing how organizations discover vulnerabilities, remediate risk and defend their environments. Realizing that potential at scale will take an ecosystem of partners who can put the technology to work. The Cyber Partnerships Team works to bring together providers of cybersecurity products, systems integrators, and our hyperscaler partners to accelerate deployment of this technology to enterprises around the world.

Within the team, Partner Applied AI Architects work with strategic partners—including global and regional system integrators, consulting and advisory firms, and technology partners—to extend OpenAI’s technical reach and help partners deliver high-quality AI solutions for our joint customers. We bring together technical strategy, partner enablement, architecture expertise, and practical deployment experience, working closely with Partnerships, Sales, Product, Engineering, Research, Security, and specialist cybersecurity teams.

About the Role

As a Cyber Partner Applied AI Architect, you will be a senior technical advisor to a portfolio of strategic cybersecurity partners and the primary technical counterpart to their leadership and delivery organizations. You will shape how partners build practices around OpenAI, develop solutions using our products, and take joint customers from unmet cybersecurity needs and technical evaluation through production adoption and measurable business impact.

You will own the technical strategy and architecture across partner engagements involving our Daybreak access programs, specialized cybersecurity products, existing non-cybersecurity product portfolio, and other agentic AI solutions. In close partnership with the broader partnerships team, you will translate joint business priorities into technical strategies, solution patterns, enablement plans, and a focused portfolio of high-value customer opportunities.

You will work directly with partners on strategic customer engagements—leading discovery, shaping architectures, navigating complex technical decisions, and helping secure technical wins—while building the partner capabilities required to deliver successfully and independently at scale.

You will remain accountable for the technical quality and outcomes of the partnership while bringing in the right specialists across deployment, implementation, security, product, enablement, and other teams when deeper expertise is needed. The role calls for strong architectural judgment, executive presence, partner leadership, and the ability to move confidently between business strategy and hands-on technical conversations.

In this role, you will:

  • Serve as the primary technical advisor and long-term technical relationship owner for cybersecurity practices across a portfolio of strategic partners, building trusted relationships with their executives, AI leaders, architects, engineering teams, and delivery organizations.

  • Partner closely with the broader partnerships team as one virtual team, aligning partner strategy, technical priorities, joint customer opportunities, and measures of success.

  • Develop the technical strategy and plan for each partner, identifying priority solutions, use cases, technical capabilities, enablement needs, delivery risks, and opportunities to drive customer adoption.

  • Assess prospective and existing partners’ cybersecurity capabilities and delivery readiness, identifying strengths, gaps, and the investments required to successfully deliver OpenAI-powered solutions.

  • Lead technical discovery with partners and joint customers to identify, qualify, and prioritize cybersecurity use-cases.

  • Develop clear Applied AI architectures spanning models, applications, enterprise data, integrations, identity, security, privacy, governance, evaluation, reliability, and deployment.

  • Guide partners through their initial and most strategic cybersecurity deployments, helping them navigate technical tradeoffs and production dependencies while ensuring solutions meet a high bar for quality, security, reliability, and responsible deployment.

  • Build partner capability and technical self-sufficiency through tailored enablement, architectural guidance, reusable solution patterns, technical workshops, and mentorship.

  • Establish clear standards and mechanisms for partner-delivered solution quality, identifying risks early and intervening when architecture, implementation, security, evaluation, or adoption issues threaten customer outcomes.

  • Orchestrate the right OpenAI specialists across Deployment Engineering, Product, Security, implementation, enablement, and domain teams while maintaining clear ownership and handoffs between OpenAI and partner delivery teams.

  • Track partner capability, joint pipeline technical progress, production adoption, usage, solution quality, and measurable customer impact to identify where additional investment or intervention is needed.

  • Identify repeatable patterns across partner engagements and turn them into architectures, playbooks, reference solutions, and best practices that allow successful approaches to scale across partners and customers.

  • Bring insights from partners and joint customers back to Product, Engineering, Research, and Partnerships, helping shape product strategy, technical guidance, and the broader OpenAI partner ecosystem.

  • Have worked successfully with global or regional system integrators, consulting firms, or other technology partners, and understand how partner organizations sell, architect, and deliver complex enterprise technology.

title: Researcher, Frontier Risk Mitigations
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

Models are becoming increasingly capable—moving from tools that assist humans to agents that can plan, execute, and adapt in the real world. Mitigating the frontier risks resulting from these capabilities is paramount to OpenAI’s ability to continue deploying models safely.

The Preparedness team is dedicated to addressing these critical risks. Our work includes:

  1. Measurement. Monitoring and predicting the evolving capabilities of frontier AI systems.

  2. Mitigation. Keeping misuse and misalignment safeguards, alignment tools, and security measures on track to adequately address extreme threats that might arise in the future.

  3. Coordination. Setting mitigation targets by maintaining OpenAI’s preparedness framework, and partnering with other staff to achieve these targets.

This is urgent, fast-paced work that has far-reaching implications for the company and for society.

About the Role

We are seeking exceptional researchers who can push the frontier of safety mitigations. You will help derisk frontier models by developing novel safety mitigations, developing and applying new techniques from domains like interpretability, control, and alignment to ensure the safety of OpenAI’s deployed models. You will play a critical role in defining how a safe AI system should look in the future at OpenAI, making a significant impact on our mission to build and deploy safe AGI.

This role requires strong technical depth and close cross-functional collaboration to ensure our safety mitigations are enforceable, scalable, and effective. We seek researchers who can partner with experts across domains such as misalignment, cybersecurity, and biology in order to develop the best possible end-to-end safety stack.

In this role, you will:

  • Work on identifying emerging AI safety risks and new methodologies for exploring and mitigating the impact of such risks

  • Build (and then continuously refine) the evaluations that enable us to assess the extent of these risks; this might include working with domain experts (be it internal or external)

  • Set research directions and strategies to make our AI systems safer, more aligned, and more robust

  • Contribute to the development of “best practices” guidelines for AI safety for OpenAI and across the industry

  • Evaluate and design effective red-teaming pipelines to examine the end-to-end robustness of our safety systems, and identify areas for future improvement.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Are excited about OpenAI’s mission of building safe, universally beneficial AGI and are aligned with OpenAI’s charter.

  • Show enthusiasm for long-term AI safety, and have thought deeply about technical paths to safe AGI.

  • Are willing to “get your hands dirty” and apply methods from domains such as interpretability, robustness, alignment, and control to make OpenAI’s models safe.

  • Bring 2+ years of experience in the field of AI safety, especially in areas like RLHF, human-AI collaboration, interpretability, or control.

  • Hold a Ph.D. or other degree in computer science, machine learning, or a related field.

  • Thrive in environments involving large-scale AI systems.

  • Possess 4+ years of research engineering experience and proficiency in Python or similar languages.

title: Applied AI Architect
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The AI Architect team partners with organizations to turn OpenAI's most capable models into meaningful, real-world impact. We work with customers across industries and digital-native businesses to identify where AI can create value, design secure and scalable solutions, and help those solutions move from early exploration into sustained production adoption. The team brings together technical strategy, customer partnership, and practical deployment expertise, working closely with Sales, Product, Engineering, Research, and specialist delivery teams.

About the Role

As an AI Architect, you will be the senior technical owner for a named portfolio of customers and the primary technical counterpart to their leadership teams. You will act as the “CTO of your book of business”, shaping each customer's AI strategy and guiding their journey from pre-sales discovery and solution evaluation through deployment, adoption, and measurable business impact.

You will own the technical account plan across ChatGPT Enterprise, the OpenAI API, Codex, and other agentic AI solutions. In partnership with the Account Director, you will translate business priorities into a focused use-case portfolio, an actionable adoption roadmap, and a clear path to durable customer value and growth. The Account Director owns commercial strategy; you own the technical strategy, customer journey, and path to production value.

You will remain accountable for the technical outcome while bringing in the right specialists across deployment, implementation, enablement, security, product, and partners to provide deeper expertise and execute work where needed. This role calls for strong industry fluency, sound architectural judgment, and the ability to move confidently between executive strategy and hands-on technical conversations.

This role is based in Seoul, South Korea. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

  • Serve as the primary technical advisor and long-term technical relationship owner for a named portfolio of existing customers and pre-sales prospects.

  • Partner with Account Directors on account strategy while owning the technical account plan, technical milestones, adoption priorities, and expansion opportunities.

  • Lead discovery with executives and technical teams to identify, qualify, and prioritize use cases tied to meaningful business outcomes.

  • Develop clear Applied AI Architectures spanning models, applications, data, integration, security, privacy, governance, evaluation, and deployment.

  • Guide customers through technical evaluations, demonstrations, workshops, prototypes, and proofs of value, securing confidence in both the solution and its path to production.

  • Maintain a focused use-case portfolio with clear decision criteria, ownership, blockers, success measures, delivery needs, and adoption plans.

  • Develop trusted relationships and technical champions across CTOs, CIOs, CISOs, AI leaders, engineering teams, and other customer stakeholders.

  • Qualify and coordinate support from Deployment Engineering, implementation, training and enablement, product and domain specialists, partners, and other delivery teams.

  • Remain accountable for technical progress and customer outcomes while ensuring delivery teams own implementation execution once engaged.

  • Track adoption, usage, account health, production readiness, and measurable customer impact, intervening early when risks threaten value realization.

  • Apply industry or digital-native expertise to recognize repeatable patterns, sharpen customer priorities, and identify relevant expansion opportunities.

  • Share customer insights with Product, Engineering, and Research, translating field learnings into better products, architecture guidance, and reusable practices.

  • Have significant experience in customer-facing technical roles such as solutions architecture, solutions engineering, technical account leadership, AI deployment, or technical customer success.

  • Have guided enterprise organizations from technical evaluation through production adoption and measurable business impact.

  • Build credibility with senior technical and business leaders while communicating equally well with hands-on engineers.

  • Bring strong software and cloud architecture foundations, including APIs, distributed systems, data integration, identity, security, and privacy.

  • Understand modern AI systems, frontier LLM models, agentic applications, model evaluation, retrieval, or enterprise AI workflows.

We are seeking a Technical Program Manager to improve developer velocity and deployment excellence across ChatGPT. You will lead durable improvements to local development, CI, testing, build systems, release trains, progressive rollout, and post-deployment validation.

title: GRC Program Manager, Audit & Controls
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Governance, Risk, and Compliance team helps ensure security and privacy are grounded in how our products and systems actually operate. Assurance Operations partners with Security, Engineering, Infrastructure, Product, Privacy, and Legal to make controls provable, risk decisions explicit, and audit readiness a result of well-designed systems.

About the Role

We are hiring a technical, product-minded GRC builder who can own consequential audits while improving the control and evidence systems behind them. You will build a reusable common control framework, use Codex to automate assurance work, validate changing system scope, and turn repeated audit friction into measurable improvements. We are looking for someone who questions inherited assumptions, solves novel problems creatively, works closely with engineers, and makes the next audit easier by improving the underlying system.

You’ll be responsible for:

  • Lead external, internal, customer, and certification audit work from scoping through evidence review, fieldwork, remediation, and closeout.

  • Build a common control framework linking risk, control intent, implementation, owner, system, environment, evidence, and applicable frameworks.

  • Validate actual scope and ownership instead of assuming last year's controls, product boundaries, or evidence remain accurate.

  • Use Codex to build and test evidence checks, control mappings, request triage, owner workflows, monitoring, and remediation reporting.

  • Partner with engineers on cloud architecture, identity, logging, data flows, software changes, vulnerabilities, and control effectiveness.

  • Design maintainable, permission-aware tools that preserve source provenance, human review, and evidence integrity.

  • Reduce repeated requests and operational burden for control owners through measurable workflow improvements.

  • Define roadmaps, decision rights, milestones, success metrics, and clear cross-functional escalations.

We’re looking for someone with:

  • Direct ownership of meaningful audit, security, customer-assurance, or regulatory outcomes.

  • Practical knowledge of control design, evidence, testing, operating effectiveness, and remediation.

  • Technical fluency across cloud systems, identity, logging, APIs, data flows, and system boundaries.

  • Ability to use Codex or comparable AI-assisted development tools to build, run, inspect, and test a working solution.

  • Experience using code, SQL, APIs, structured data, automation, or data workflows to solve an operational problem.

  • Ability to design reusable cross-framework controls without erasing framework-specific test and evidence requirements.

  • First-principles curiosity, creative problem solving, intellectual humility, and the ability to update when facts change.

  • Product and program judgment: define the user, scope, milestones, ownership, adoption, and measurable outcome.

  • Clear, constructive partnership with Security, Engineering, Infrastructure, Product, Privacy, Legal, and audit teams.

  • Frameworks such as SOC 2, ISO 27001/27017, PCI DSS, NIST, or FedRAMP are helpful; a specific degree, certification, or prior access to internal OpenAI tools is not required.

title: Model Policy Manager, Agentic Safety
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

Our Safety Systems team is at the forefront of OpenAI's mission to build and deploy safe AGI, driving our commitment to AI safety and fostering a culture of trust and transparency.

Within Safety Systems, the Model Policy team works to ensure that increasingly capable models behave safely and reliably in real-world environments. We investigate emerging model failures, define the behavior models should exhibit instead, and develop the data, evaluations, monitoring, and safeguards needed to improve and validate that behavior. Our work connects alignment research with the practical challenges of training and deploying frontier models.

About the Role

In this role, you will shape how OpenAI understands and addresses real-world risks that emerge from model misalignment as models become more autonomous and operate over longer horizons. You will investigate how misaligned behavior emerges across extended trajectories - including when models persist toward the wrong objective, take unsafe shortcuts, lose track of instructions, exploit weaknesses in their environment, or circumvent constraints - and translate these insights into behavioral policies, evaluations, monitoring, and safeguards. This role is ideal for someone who wants to turn alignment and safety concerns into concrete, empirically grounded improvements to frontier AI systems.

This role is based in our San Francisco office. We offer relocation support to new employees, and we use a hybrid model: three days in the office per week with optional work from home on Thursdays and Fridays.

Your Responsibilities:

  • Identify vulnerabilities that emerge as models interact with tools, data, and external systems, and translate them into model- and system-level safeguards.

  • Develop threat models and empirical frameworks for understanding harmful outcomes from misaligned behavior.

  • Build frameworks for understanding harmful outcomes arising from model misalignment.

  • Identify the underlying behaviors and system conditions that drive those outcomes.

  • Turn findings into policy frameworks, evaluation criteria, online measurement and safeguards.

  • Develop human data campaigns and gold sets to ground measurement and evaluation of emerging behaviors and risks.

  • Partner with research, engineering, security, and product teams to shape model and system safety, balancing difficult trade-offs between safety, utility, and business risk.

  • Inform deployment decisions, system cards, safeguards reports, and OpenAI’s broader approach to agentic safety.

  • Build monitoring approaches that detect regressions and emerging risks after deployment.

We’re seeking someone who:

  • Brings a strong background in AI agent safety, privacy, security, cybersecurity, or adjacent fields, with the adversarial mindset needed to investigate real-world harmful outcomes.

  • Has demonstrated interest in AI alignment and a strong understanding of the technical drivers of misaligned model behavior.

  • Has enough technical fluency to work directly with evaluation and training data, understand what the data is showing, and identify limitations, patterns, and opportunities for deeper investigation.

  • Is comfortable working hands-on with model data and evaluation results, including inspecting examples, analyzing failure patterns, assessing data quality, and distinguishing policy failures from grader, model, or system failures.

  • Uses empirical evidence to develop and refine safety policies and safeguards.

  • Can translate complex or ambiguous alignment risks into precise behavioral expectations and measurable evaluation criteria.

  • Works effectively across research, engineering, security, product, and policy.

  • Communicates clearly about complex and uncertain technical risks.

  • Enjoys fast-paced, collaborative research environments where priorities shift as models, evidence, and risks change.

 

Our relevant publications:

  • Safety and alignment in an era of long-horizon models

title: Threat Detection and Response Engineering Manager
descriptionHtml:
About the team

OpenAI’s mission depends on developing and deploying powerful AI responsibly. Security makes that possible by protecting our research, people, products, and users while enabling progress. We defend sensitive research and other intellectual property, customer data, and the infrastructure behind frontier AI—from GPU supercomputing and multicloud environments to datacenters and emerging agent systems. Threat Detection Engineering builds and operates the detections and investigative workflows that turn adversary activity into effective response.

About the role

We’re looking for a hands-on technical leader to guide the engineers who identify and investigate threats to OpenAI and build the capabilities to contain them. You’ll hire and develop engineers, set technical direction, and prioritize risks to OpenAI’s intellectual property, customer data, and critical infrastructure.

Your team will take an agent-first approach across the detection and response lifecycle, using OpenAI’s models to develop detections, triage signals, investigate suspicious activity, and support bounded response and continuous improvement. You’ll turn advances in model capability into dependable defenses, own their effectiveness, and work with security, research, and infrastructure partners to ensure findings lead to effective action. You’ll establish where agents can act independently and where human judgment and approval are essential.

In this role, you will:

  • Hire, coach, and develop engineers. Set clear expectations, provide regular feedback, grow technical leadership, and build a team that reviews work rigorously and learns from missed detections and noisy signals.

  • Set a threat-informed roadmap. Prioritize detection work based on how external and internal actors could target the systems where we train and evaluate frontier models, the production services that run inference and power our products worldwide, the datacenter hardware and networks that support both, and the devices, identities, and applications employees rely on. Balance investment in emerging threats with closing known coverage gaps and keeping existing detections effective.

  • Own detection and investigation as a complete workflow. Embed agent-driven triage and investigation in the detections your team operates. Surface findings when the evidence points to a likely threat that warrants action. When a finding warrants formal incident response, bring the evidence to the Security Incident Response Team (SIRT) and support the investigation SIRT leads.

  • Build response and containment capabilities tailored to our infrastructure. Work with infrastructure and system owners to develop and test the controls responders need to contain threats in their environments. Define when human approval is required and how to verify that containment worked.

  • Apply models across the detection engineering lifecycle. Use OpenAI’s models to help develop threat hypotheses, author and test detections, deploy and tune them, and incorporate investigation findings into better coverage. Evaluate the effectiveness of individual agents and the complete workflows they support.

  • Turn model advances into tested defenses. Prototype new approaches using OpenAI’s models, evaluate them against realistic adversary behavior and analyst baselines, and move successful experiments into production. Use operational evidence to identify model limitations and partner with Research and Engineering to address them.

  • Anticipate emerging threats. Translate adversary intelligence and incident findings into testable detection hypotheses. Work with researchers and infrastructure owners on risks specific to a frontier AI lab, such as increasingly capable agents operating across systems with access to sensitive research. Determine what evidence would reveal compromise and what response would be effective.

  • Establish the visibility needed to detect, investigate, and respond. Partner with Security Observability and infrastructure owners to define telemetry and forensic data requirements. Drive improvements where missing evidence, unreliable data, or limited controls prevent the team from identifying threats or taking effective action.

  • Engineer for measurable security outcomes. Use replay, adversarial validation, and regression testing to assess whether workflows find intended threats, distinguish benign activity, and reach defensible conclusions. Establish code review, documentation, staged rollout, monitoring, and rollback practices. Measure coverage, investigation accuracy, time to identify threats, and effectiveness of response.

  • Contribute during incidents. The Security Incident Response Team (SIRT) leads formal incident response. Your team contributes investigative expertise and uses incident findings to improve detections.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Think like an adversary and demand evidence as a defender. You question whether apparent coverage would survive a determined attacker, distinguish plausible explanations from supported conclusions, and stay accountable for threats that existing tools and playbooks miss.

  • Have managed security or software engineers and can demonstrate how you have hired, coached, developed technical judgment, and improved a team’s ability to deliver.

  • Are a hands-on builder who can prototype tools, write and review code, and guide engineers through complex detection, investigation, and response designs.

  • Bring strong AI fluency and have built systems that test how models or agents can improve cyber defense. You have evaluated real security workflows against meaningful baselines and can explain what improved, what failed, and what you changed. You understand model failure modes and design reliable workflows with bounded permissions and clear human decision points.

  • Have built or operated threat detections and led technical investigations. You understand adversary tradecraft and can assess evidence, scope, and uncertainty across complex environments.

  • Understand how identity, endpoint, cloud, Kubernetes, and infrastructure telemetry supports investigations. You can reason about response and containment in unfamiliar systems and work with their owners to build practical capabilities.

  • Have used testing and operational feedback to improve security outcomes. You can explain tradeoffs among coverage, accuracy, speed, and human workload, and choose measures that reflect whether threats are being found and addressed.

  • Can build a focused roadmap and strong cross-functional partnerships in a rapidly changing environment. You enable researchers and engineers to move quickly while following through on security requirements and dependable operations.
