title: Dedicated Support Engineer - Dublin
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI’s User Operations team shepherds our customers’ adoption of AI and ensures that our customers' product experience is nothing short of exceptional. We are building the very first post-AGI support team. We resolve complex issues, provide technical guidance, and support customers in maximizing value and adoption from deploying our products. We work closely with Sales, Technical Success, Product, Engineering and others, to deliver the best possible experience to our customers at scale. OpenAI's customers represent a range of diverse backgrounds and maturity, from early-stage startups to established global enterprises.

About the Role

The Support Engineering team works closely with Engineering, Product, Technical Success, Go-to-Market, and other teams to deliver an exceptional experience for our most strategic customers. We combine deep technical troubleshooting with durable customer context, proactive reliability work, and clear ownership during critical moments. We use automation, agents, and our own technology to help build the future of technical support.

We’re looking for experienced, deeply curious technical problem-solvers to serve as trusted support partners for our Premium Support customers. You’ll work directly with customers on novel, ambiguous, and high-impact technical issues, using logs, telemetry, reproduction, and systems-level investigation to isolate causes and drive issues toward resolution.

Beyond resolving individual issues, you’ll use your deep understanding of OpenAI’s infrastructure and products, together with each customer’s architecture and operating context, to anticipate risk and make their workloads more resilient over time. You’ll proactively monitor integrations, identify emerging failure patterns and architectural breakpoints, and work with customers and internal teams to address them before they become incidents. Success means that as a customer’s workloads mature and scale, the day-to-day effort required to support them decreases through better monitoring, runbooks, automation, and preventative improvements.

In this role, you will:

  • Work directly with Premium Support customers to troubleshoot their most complex technical issues, including API failures, integration challenges, authentication errors, unexpected product behavior, performance degradation, and production incidents.

  • Provide end-to-end technical ownership by analyzing logs and system behavior, reproducing errors, testing hypotheses, and isolating the likely failure domain. Where possible, you’ll identify the root cause before escalating to Engineering; where that is not possible, you’ll provide a clear hypothesis and the evidence needed to accelerate Engineering’s investigation.

  • Become a trusted expert on OpenAI’s products and systems, serving as a critical escalation point and a technical backstop for our most strategic customers.

  • Own the customer-specific response to high-impact incidents. You’ll assess severity and business impact, initiate the appropriate response path, coordinate cross-functional responders, maintain clear ownership, and ensure issues move through mitigation, resolution, and post-incident follow-through.

  • Communicate clearly and proactively during periods of uncertainty, providing accurate updates to customer technical teams, business stakeholders, executives, and internal partners.

  • Develop a detailed understanding of each customer’s architecture, integrations, dependencies, critical workloads, and operational constraints. You’ll document this context and make it accessible to Support, Product, and Engineering teams.

  • Partner with Go-to-Market and Technical Success teams to understand the business importance of customer workloads and ensure that relevant commercial context informs severity, prioritization, and communication without bypassing established support processes.

  • Represent Support Engineering in relevant customer meetings, including QBRs, and partner closely with account teams to communicate technical health, surface risks and blockers early, coordinate follow-up, and provide customers and internal stakeholders with clear, proactive updates.

  • Monitor customer integrations and support trends to identify emerging risks, recurring failure patterns, and readiness gaps before they become major escalations.

  • Prepare for important launches, migrations, traffic increases, and business events by developing account-specific runbooks, validating escalation paths, coordinating support readiness, and providing heightened monitoring where needed.

  • Lead or contribute to incident reviews and postmortems, identify opportunities to prevent recurrence, and track corrective actions through closure.

  • Translate recurring customer pain into clear, evidence-backed feedback for Product and Engineering, with a particular focus on improving the reliability and performance of existing products, integrations, and deployments.

  • Turn what you learn from customer investigations into scalable improvements, including troubleshooting guides, monitoring, internal tooling, support workflows, and AI-powered automation.

  • Help shape the operating model, technical standards, and tooling for Premium Support as the function grows globally.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have significant experience in Support Engineering, Solutions Engineering, Solutions Architecture, or another role involving hands-on diagnosis of complex production issues.

  • Have expert-level troubleshooting skills and a strong track record of resolving ambiguous technical problems across APIs, distributed systems, cloud infrastructure, and enterprise integrations.

  • Are comfortable working with logs, metrics, traces, API requests, authentication flows, and customer-provided code or configurations to understand system behavior and test hypotheses.

  • Have experience leading or playing a central role in customer-impacting incidents, including severity assessment, technical coordination, stakeholder communication, root-cause analysis, and post-incident follow-through.

  • Can write code or scripts to reproduce issues, interrogate systems, automate repetitive work, and improve internal tools. Experience with Python, JavaScript, or similar languages is valuable.

  • Can communicate complex technical issues clearly to engineers, customer technical teams, business stakeholders, and senior leaders—especially when information is incomplete or evolving.

  • Build strong, high-trust relationships with customers and cross-functional partners while maintaining clear and scalable ownership boundaries.

  • Look beyond the immediate issue to identify patterns, improve the system, and prevent the same problem from recurring.

  • Thrive in ambiguity, update quickly as new information emerges, and are willing to learn whatever is needed to get the job done.

  • Bring a humble, team-first mindset, strong judgment, and a genuine eagerness to help both customers and colleagues succeed.

  • Are excited to use OpenAI’s products, agents, and emerging AI capabilities to transform how technical support operates at scale.

OpenAI’s Sales team partners with advertisers to understand their businesses, develop meaningful advertising solutions, and drive long-term growth on the platform while maintaining strong standards for user trust and platform integrity.

title: IT Logistics Lead
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

Employee Technology & Experience helps people at OpenAI do their most ambitious work. Across Helpdesk, Executive Support, Systems Operations, Logistics and audiovisual services, we make technology simple, reliable and secure. Employee needs guide what we build, improve and eliminate.

IT Logistics keeps employees equipped, from day 1 readiness to timely replacements and self-service peripherals. We manage the full equipment lifecycle and improve access to hardware as employee needs evolve.

About the Role

We’re hiring an IT Logistics Lead to manage the team that keeps OpenAI employees equipped for their most important work. You’ll run daily operations, evaluate new hardware and introduce equipment and services that address unmet needs.

You’ll own the hardware and peripheral catalog, fulfillment programs, asset management systems and regional operating models. You’ll deliver on IT’s promise: equipment ready on day 1 globally, choices suited to each employee’s location and work, self-service employees trust, and accurate records of what we own, where it is and who has it.

This is a hands-on people management role. You’ll coach team members, manage performance and work alongside them on execution and escalations. With your manager, you’ll set priorities and plan capacity. As customer zero, you’ll use OpenAI products to solve unresolved logistics problems, continually improving accuracy and shortening lead times.

In this role, you will:

  • Own a hardware and peripheral catalog that keeps pace with employee needs, with new equipment options and devices ready for use with current, validated software images and configurations.

  • Deliver day 1 readiness globally, with equipment suited to each employee’s location and work. Ensure timely fulfillment, refreshes, replacements, loaners, telecom and mobility, and high-risk travel services as offices and programs expand.

  • Own and scale the employee IT vending machine program and other self-service channels as services employees trust, with the right peripherals available, machines working every time and tightly managed shrinkage.

  • Own asset accountability across the full lifecycle, with 100% accurate records that reconcile to physical inventory and trusted chain of custody from receipt through recovery, reuse and secure disposition.

  • Own forecasting, capacity and logistics performance to continually improve accuracy, shorten lead times and keep equipment available. Control lifecycle costs, reduce excess stock and waste, and maintain service through supply disruptions.

  • Use OpenAI products, including Codex and agents, as customer zero to solve previously unresolved logistics problems and improve accuracy, speed and scale, with appropriate evaluation, security and human oversight.

  • Manage and develop team members so each person builds skills, takes ownership and delivers excellent work. Build team and delivery partner capability that sustains quality and consistency as demand grows.

  • Scale service globally with accountable regional partners and repeatable operations that meet local needs while maintaining speed, inventory accuracy and a consistent employee experience.

  • Keep daily operations reliable as demand changes, with timely escalation resolution, capacity and commitments aligned with your manager, and clear decision ownership across engineering, security, support, workplace, finance and procurement.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

  • Led inventory and fulfillment across multiple sites or regions, owning forecasting, delivery partners, service performance and cost, with sustained improvements in accuracy, reconciliation, shrinkage, availability and lead times.

  • Delivered automation and AI-enabled workflows used in daily operations, including solutions to previously unresolved problems. You can explain your contribution, measurable results, reliability testing, security controls and human oversight.

  • Managed people through rising demand and changing priorities, with responsibility for goals, feedback, performance and development. Your coaching helped individuals build skills, take ownership and improve their work.

  • Launched services that met employee or customer needs, balancing usability, cost, security and control. You align partners, make sound technical and business decisions, communicate candidly and own adoption and results.

descriptionHtml:

OpenAI builds powerful AI systems like ChatGPT, the OpenAI API, and enterprise products that serve millions of users across the globe. As we scale, securing our infrastructure, protecting sensitive data, and meeting global compliance standards are essential to our success and societal impact.

Security at OpenAI is a cross-cutting function that spans infrastructure, applied engineering, legal, policy, and product. We’re seeking a Senior Technical Program Manager to drive cross-functional security, privacy, IT and compliance initiatives at the intersection of infrastructure, product, and policy. You will execute complex programs that reduce internal data access, prevent misuse, and ship security capabilities. You will focus your efforts on the most critical initiatives within Security, crossing the spectrum of insider threat, information security, physical security, and information technology challenges.

We are building the Defense Factory to help enterprises find and fix security vulnerabilities with AI. We build infrastructure that enables AI agents to work in secure, customer-controlled cloud environments, with the context, tools, and controls they need to investigate security findings, carry out approved actions, and verify results.

Our focus is turning AI capabilities into reliable security outcomes, starting with finding and fixing vulnerabilities and expanding into investigation, detection, and response. title: Engineering Manager, Preparedness
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The Preparedness Engineering team is responsible for building and operating safeguards for frontier model risks, to safely enable advanced capabilities while detecting and limiting harm.

About the Role

We’re looking for an engineering manager to lead a team building software systems that detect and prevent harmful misuse of frontier AI models—before incidents occur. This is a builder’s role: you’ll lead engineers shipping production services, detection pipelines, and mitigation mechanisms that protect frontier model integrity and reduce high-severity misuse risk.

While this work intersects with frontier model development, security and risk, we’re explicitly seeking someone with a software engineering foundation who is comfortable building reliable systems that can operate at billions of users scale.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

title: Researcher, Misalignment Monitoring Lead
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI's Safety Research organization works to ensure that our most capable AI models can be deployed safely and responsibly. As frontier models become increasingly capable and autonomous, developing reliable ways to monitor their behavior, identify emerging risks, and evaluate the effectiveness of safety systems becomes increasingly important.

Our work focuses on advancing the research and evaluation methods needed to understand model behavior and ensure that monitoring systems remain effective as model capabilities evolve. We combine rigorous empirical research with practical safety interventions, working closely with research, engineering, and deployment teams to translate findings into improvements across OpenAI's models and products.

About the Role

We are looking for a senior researcher to lead technical work on misalignment monitoring for frontier AI systems. You will develop methods to evaluate the effectiveness of AI monitors, understand their limitations, and improve our ability to detect and stop concerning model behavior reliably.

This role combines research leadership with hands-on technical execution. You will set research priorities, design rigorous evaluations, investigate monitoring failures, and develop approaches for stress-testing and improving monitoring systems. A key focus will be understanding where monitors produce false positives, miss important behaviors, or become less effective as models grow more capable.

You will work closely with researchers and engineers across OpenAI to turn monitoring research into practical improvements to our safety systems. We are looking for someone with strong research judgment, technical depth, and the ability to independently drive ambiguous problems from initial investigation through measurable results.

In this role, you will:

  • Lead the research and technical direction for evaluating and improving the misalignment monitoring of frontier AI systems.

  • Design and execute rigorous evaluations that measure monitor effectiveness, identify failure modes, and assess the reliability of monitoring signals.

  • Develop methods to stress-test and red-team monitors, including identifying behaviors that evade detection or expose weaknesses in existing approaches.

  • Investigate false positives, missed detections, and other monitoring failures to improve the accuracy and usefulness of safety evaluations.

  • Build scalable evaluation frameworks and experimental tools that enable ongoing measurement of monitoring performance as model capabilities evolve.

  • Translate research findings into actionable improvements, working with partner teams to strengthen monitoring systems and inform broader safety decisions.

  • Establish research priorities and guide technical execution, balancing foundational research questions with practical deployment needs.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have a strong background in machine learning research, particularly in model evaluations, AI safety, alignment, robustness, or related areas.

  • Have demonstrated the ability to lead technically challenging research projects, from identifying important questions through designing experiments and delivering results.

  • Bring strong experimental judgment and understand how to design evaluations that are rigorous, reproducible, and difficult to game.

  • Have hands-on experience building or evaluating machine learning systems, including working with large language models or other frontier AI systems.

  • Enjoy investigating complex failure modes and developing methods to distinguish meaningful safety signals from misleading measurements.

  • Are comfortable working on open-ended research problems where the right methodology or success criteria may not be obvious at the outset.

  • Combine strong research instincts with practical engineering ability and can independently build experiments, analyze results, and iterate quickly.

  • Communicate technical findings clearly and enjoy collaborating across research, engineering, and safety teams.

  • Are motivated by OpenAI's mission and the challenge of developing reliable oversight mechanisms for increasingly capable AI systems.

Nice to have:

  • Experience with AI monitoring, automated evaluations, adversarial testing, or red-teaming.

  • Research experience in scalable oversight, AI control, model behavior analysis, or interpretability.

  • Experience developing monitoring or evaluation systems that are used in real-world deployments.

  • A track record of technical research leadership, including mentoring researchers or coordinating cross-functional research initiatives.

title: Culture & Community Communications lead
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Product & Research Communications team helps people understand our technology, what it makes possible, and how to use it. We bring new products and research to the world and tell stories about the people making these tools their own.

We work closely with our Culture & Community Engagement team to connect our products with people’s interests, ambitions, and everyday lives. Together, we help more people discover what they can create, learn, and do with AI—and bring their experiences back into how we communicate.

About the Role

We’re looking for a Community Communications Lead to bring OpenAI’s products closer to communities and help their stories reach a wider audience. Sitting on the Product & Research Communications team, you’ll work hand in hand with the Culture & Community team to shape narratives, develop earned media opportunities, and amplify community-driven stories across organic communications channels.

You’ll be involved from the beginning of campaigns and community programs, bringing ideas that strengthen the story, cultural relevance, and opportunities for participation. Working closely with Culture & Community Engagement leaders, you’ll contribute communications strategy while respecting their ownership of campaign and creative decisions.

You’ll also connect individual campaigns, partnerships, and community moments into a broader story that develops over time. You’ll have the judgment to know when the work has earned a larger conversation—and the relationships and storytelling skills to make it happen.

We’re looking for someone with cultural curiosity, strong editorial taste, initiative, judgment and an entrepreneurial approach. You understand what makes people care and how community trust is built. You keep our claims grounded, can navigate skepticism about AI and understand how a story can invite people to take part.

title: Software Engineer, Compute Infrastructure
descriptionHtml:
About the Team:

Compute Infrastructure builds the platform that turns enormous amounts of compute into a reliable engine for frontier AI. We design, provision, schedule, operate, and optimize the systems that connect accelerators, CPUs, networks, storage, data centers, orchestration software, agent infrastructure, developer tools, and observability into one coherent experience for researchers and product teams.

Our work spans the entire stack: capacity planning and cluster lifecycle, bare-metal automation, distributed systems, Kubernetes and scheduling, deep system optimization, high-performance networking, storage, fleet health, reliability, workload profiling, benchmarking, and the developer experience that lets teams use enormous compute systems with confidence. At this scale, small improvements to communication, scheduling, hardware efficiency, or debugging workflows can compound into meaningful research velocity. We are hiring across Compute Infrastructure rather than for a single narrow team, and we use this opening to match strong engineers to the problems where they can have the most leverage.

About the Role

We are looking for engineers who want to build the compute platform behind OpenAI's research and products. You may not be the strongest in low-level systems, high-performance computing, distributed infrastructure, reliability, CaaS, agent infrastructure, developer platforms, tooling, or the user experience around infrastructure. What matters is that you can reason carefully about complex systems, write durable software, and raise the quality and velocity of the people around you.

Depending on your background and interests, you might work close to hardware, close to users, on CaaS and agent infrastructure, or on the control planes and data planes in between. You could help bring new supercomputing capacity online, optimize training workloads from profiler traces and benchmarks, improve NCCL and collective communication behavior, reason about GPUs, NICs, topology, firmware, thermals, and failure modes, or design abstractions that make heterogeneous clusters feel like one coherent platform.

We do not expect every candidate to have worked at every layer. Some engineers will go deep on systems performance, kernel or runtime behavior, large-scale networking protocols, RDMA, NCCL, GPU hardware behavior, benchmarking, scheduling, or hardware reliability; others will make the platform more usable through APIs, tools, workflows, and developer experience. The common thread is strong engineering judgment and excitement about making enormous compute systems faster, more reliable, and easier to use.

This is a general opening for Compute Infrastructure. We will consider candidates for teams across Compute Infrastructure and match you based on your strengths, the problems that motivate you, and where the infrastructure needs are highest.

Where you might work

  • Compute Foundations: Build the low-level platform primitives that make heterogeneous hardware, providers, and data centers repeatable, automatable, and operable at scale.

  • Fleet / Orchestration: Turn raw capacity into reliable, efficient clusters and scheduling systems that researchers and product teams can use with minimal friction and great experience.

  • Core Network Engineering: Build and operate the high-performance networking fabrics, protocols, and observability needed for the largest training and serving workloads.

  • Hardware Health and Observability: Detect, diagnose, remediate, and prevent hardware and fleet-health issues so usable compute stays high across providers and accelerator generations.

  • Storage: Build scalable, performant, durable storage abstractions that keep data movement and storage access from becoming a bottleneck to research or products.

  • Agent Infrastructure: Build sandboxed execution infrastructure for agentic workloads across research and production, with strong isolation, reliability, and scale.

In this role, you will:

title: Research Engineer / Research Scientist, Post-Training — Collective Alignment (User Signals)
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The Collective Alignment (User Signals) team is a post-training research team working at the intersection of data science, human feedback, and reinforcement learning. We develop methods for learning from real-world user interactions to build AI systems that deliver lasting value, helping people learn, grow, and accomplish increasingly complex goals with ChatGPT.

Learning from user feedback presents fundamental research challenges: signals are often noisy, biased, and difficult to interpret, and improvements in offline metrics do not always translate into better experiences for users. Our team develops scientific approaches to understanding these signals and translating them into improvements in model behavior through evaluations, reward modeling, and post-training.

About the Role

As a Research Engineer or Research Scientist, you will investigate how AI systems can learn from human feedback and real-world usage to better serve users over time.

You will develop new approaches to extracting meaningful learning signals from complex user interactions and incorporating those signals into model training.

This role requires strong deep learning research skills, scientific rigor, and curiosity about how people interact with AI. You will design controlled experiments and ablations, critically examine the relationship between offline evaluations and online model behavior, and work closely with research, product, and data science teams to understand whether improvements translate into meaningful value for users.

In this role, you will:

  • Develop novel methods for learning from human feedback and user interaction signals.

  • Research approaches to incorporating feedback into reward modeling, reinforcement learning, and post-training.

  • Design rigorous experiments and ablation studies to isolate the effects of new data, objectives, and training methods.

  • Develop offline evaluations and investigate their relationship with online experiments and real-world user outcomes.

  • Analyze unexpected results, investigate discrepancies between evaluation metrics and user behavior, and develop hypotheses to guide further research.

  • Evaluate tradeoffs and regressions to improve targeted model behaviors while preserving broader capabilities.

  • Collaborate with research, alignment, product, and data science teams.

  • Implement and debug experiments across large-scale deep learning research systems.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have a strong background in deep learning research through academic or industry experience.

  • Have demonstrated research ability through publications or substantive research contributions in deep learning or LLM post-training.

  • Have experience developing new machine learning methods and evaluating them through rigorous, hypothesis-driven experimentation.

  • Think critically about experimental design, measurement, and what evaluation results do and do not establish about model behavior.

  • Are comfortable designing ablations, investigating surprising results, and reasoning about the relationship between offline metrics and real-world outcomes.

  • Have strong programming skills and experience working with complex ML codebases.

  • Are curious about how people interact with AI and how those interactions can inform better models.

Nice to have:

  • Experience with RLHF, reinforcement learning, or modern LLM post-training.

  • Research or demonstrated interest in AI alignment, human feedback, or user signals.

  • Experience with online experimentation, evaluation methodology, or learning from noisy and biased feedback.

title: Researcher, Multimodal Safety
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI is at the center of some of the highest-impact multimodal work in AI. ChatGPT serves a massive global audience, and enables diverse interactions via text, speech, and visuals. As interactive surfaces grow, models also need to adapt to emerging harm, understand user intent and situational context, and respond appropriately.

The Chat and Multimodal Safety team is responsible for ensuring that OpenAI’s increasingly multimodal models and products behave safely across these experiences. We develop the research, training methods, and evaluations needed to make these experiences safe. Our work sits at the frontier of responsibly deploying powerful AI, in close partnership with Personal AGI, io, model training, and product teams.

About the Role

As a Researcher on the Chat and Multimodal Safety team, you will help shape how frontier models perceive and reason the world, and translate that understanding into safe behavior.

We’re looking for people who combine deep technical expertise with strong safety judgment. Strong candidates often bridge perception and language: they may have built vision-language models, worked on modality fusion or image encoders, developed multimodal post-training or evaluations, or advanced safety for image, video, or audio systems.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

  • Define and advance multimodal safety research for text, vision, and audio, connecting perception and semantic understanding to safe model behavior.

  • Build training and evaluation methods for VLMs, including post-training, safety evals, and interventions that help models respond safely and appropriately in varied contexts.

  • Collaborate closely with Personal AGI, Consumer Devices, and product/model teams to translate research into safer ambient, embedded, and personalized multimodal experiences.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have a track record of building or advancing multimodal models, with depth in vision-language models, video understanding, image generation, audio, or multimodal reasoning—and fluency across both perception and language.

  • Understand how multimodal systems work end to end, from encoders, projection layers, and modality fusion to cross-modal reasoning, scaling, and inference tradeoffs.

  • Have improved frontier model behavior through post-training, using approaches such as SFT, RL, data curation, synthetic data, evaluation, and rigorous error analysis.

  • Bring strong research and engineering judgment to open-ended safety problems: you can form testable hypotheses, design decisive experiments and evaluations, diagnose model failures, and translate findings into robust improvements.

title: GRC Technical Program Manager, Product Lifecycle Assurance
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) is foundational to Security delivering mission outcomes at OpenAI. The GRC team provides security assurances and builds compliance for OpenAI’s technology, people, and products. We are technical in what we build but operational in how we do our work, and we partner deeply with Product, Security, Legal, Privacy, GTM, and Field Security to help OpenAI move quickly while maintaining trust with customers, auditors, regulators, and the public.

About the Role

We are looking for an experienced Product Lifecycle Assurance IC to help scale OpenAI’s GRC function across our product stack to ensure products address customer and regulatory compliance requirements at launch and regressions are detected promptly and corrected.

You will partner closely with Product, Security, Legal, and Privacy teams to make sure OpenAI can move quickly while maintaining our security, privacy and compliance claims and giving customers, auditors, and regulators assurance about how OpenAI handles user data. You are responsible for product assurance end-to-end from inception to post-launch (continuous) monitoring. You leverage existing workflows, reviews, and data and enhance, augment and build the components needed to create an end-to-end product assurance program.

This role is not about supporting SOC or ISO audits; it's a highly cross-functional and deeply technical operations role to ensure that OAI products meet the compliance bar at launch, regressions are prevented and detected, and our compliance state can be evidenced. This role also helps ensure that our product launch governance program operates effectively across key safety, privacy, legal and security stakeholders and lessons-learned from incidents and regressions are used to improve the program.

You or in partnership with engineering teams, build key controls in our infrastructure stack, developer workflows and launch tooling to provide developers with guardrails, perform CI/CD conformance checks, and surface launches that need GRC guidance. You ensure that teams have the information needed to design and launch safety and meet them where they are. You exercise sound judgement in making high-stakes decisions related to product launch risk and controls.

You are comfortable working in high velocity, low friction development environments. Your work goes across team boundaries and you assist and enable other teams to realize product assurance objectives. You should be comfortable with complex (Kubernetes) system architectures and dataflows, working with engineering teams to understand what could go wrong and where and how controls should be applied. You should be comfortable working with Privacy engineering and Data Science to understand data maps and database schemas and leverage existing processes and controls to further product assurance goals.

 

We’re looking for people who bring:

 

  • Strong technical product lifecycle assurance and security and privacy compliance experience working in high velocity, low friction development environments.

  • Experience building technical controls, metrics, monitoring tools, CI/CD tooling, high-fidelity risk signals and dashboards to meet product assurance goals

  • Ability to run an end-to-end, cross-functional, product assurance program applying judgement where what type of process or controls should be in place to meet a high assurance bar

  • Capacity to shift product assurance to the left in the product development cycle with just-in-time controls, guidance, guardrails and responsible friction for developers

  • Low ego outcome oriented mindset to achieve the product assurance goal required for OAI’s mission

  • Strong technical cross-functional leadership and don’t work in a vacuum - they influence, align and direct partner teams to achieve product assurance goals.

  • Exercise sound judgement in making high-stakes decisions related to product launch risk and controls.

  • Curiosity about using AI and agents to streamline product assurance workflows while preserving reliable evidence and sound judgment.

You’ll be responsible for:

  • The end-to-end effective operation of OAI’s product assurance program from product development to post-launch (continuous) monitoring

  • Owning the GRC product assurance program, providing governance over Safety, Deployment, Security, Legal reviews to ensure we effectively surface product risk and design scalable mitigations

  • Driving cross-function collaboration and accountability in all aspects of the product assurance program

  • Building controls and low-friction, scalable processes in our infrastructure stack, developer workflows and launch tooling to ensure effective product assurance

  • Ensuring that teams have the guidance needed to design and launch safety and meet them where they are

  • Ensuring compliance, security and privacy claims and maps to verifiable controls

  • Recognizing how the product lifecycle assurance program fits into the large organizational objectives and when to build and when to influence and maintain strong partnerships with partner teams and influence roadmaps to further assurance goals

title: Full Stack Engineer, Enterprise Expansions
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

Enterprise Expansions is part of OpenAI’s Enterprise Engineering organization. We help organizations make ChatGPT Work part of everyday work, from discovering what it can do to building useful agentic workflows. Our goal is to help employees move from their first chat to confidently using AI to get work done.

Our full stack work focuses on two workstreams:

  • Agentic Activation: Help first-time chat users become effective agent users within their organizations. Bring organizational context into ChatGPT and build personalized onboarding, product education, and experiments that help people adopt agents in daily workflows.

  • Work Discovery: Make relevant skills, plugins, capabilities, and context easy for knowledge workers to find and ready to use. Build discovery experiences across the frontend and backend.

Across both workstreams, we ship quickly, learn from customers, and use experiments to improve adoption.

About the Role

We’re looking for a full stack engineer with strong frontend skills, product instincts, and UX and design taste. The work ranges from activating first-time users to helping knowledge workers discover the capabilities and context they need to make ChatGPT useful in their daily workflows.

You’ll own projects from early prototypes through production and iteration, shaping interactions and building the backend services that support them. This role is a fit for someone who cares about the details of how a product feels and can turn an ambiguous user problem into a simple, polished experience. This role is based in San Francisco.

In this role, you will:

  • Build personalized onboarding and product education that help first-time ChatGPT users adopt agentic workflows.

  • Create discovery experiences that make relevant skills, plugins, capabilities, and organizational context easy for knowledge workers to find and use.

  • Shape product flows and implement polished interfaces, with careful attention to interaction details, accessibility, and responsiveness.

  • Own the frontend and backend of product features, including the services, APIs, and data flows that support the user experience.

  • Design and run product experiments, measure adoption, and use the results to improve how people get started and build lasting habits.

  • Learn directly from customers, identify work that agents can take on, and turn those insights into prototypes and production features.

Your background might look something like:

  • 7+ years of professional software engineering experience, excluding internships, building and shipping user-facing products.

  • Strong frontend engineering skills and experience building production web applications with modern frameworks.

  • Strong UX and design taste, demonstrated through intuitive product flows, thoughtful interaction design, and attention to visual detail.

  • Experience building backend services, APIs, and data models, with the ability to work independently across the stack.

  • A track record of owning features from problem definition and technical design through implementation, launch, and iteration.

  • Strong product judgment and experience using customer feedback and product data to decide what to build and how to improve it.

  • Sound engineering fundamentals and a practical approach to testing, performance, accessibility, reliability, and maintainability.

  • Ability to collaborate closely with designers, product managers, and engineers, and make progress when problems and priorities are still taking shape.

title: Compensation Programs & Operations Lead
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Compensation team helps attract, reward, and retain the people advancing our mission to ensure that artificial general intelligence benefits all of humanity. We develop compensation strategies and programs that support a rapidly evolving business, combining market insight, sound judgment, and thoughtful execution. We partner across People, Finance, Legal, and the business to deliver programs that employees and leaders can understand and trust.

About the Role

We’re looking for a Compensation Programs & Operations Lead to own the end-to-end program management of our cyclical and ad hoc compensation programs globally. You will turn compensation priorities into executable plans and lead delivery from initial scoping through launch, reconciliation, and continuous improvement.

This is a senior, hands-on role for a compensation subject-matter expert who is energized by operations and E2E program ownership. You should bring experience across compensation operations analysis, compensation analysis, business partnership, and program management. Having done this work yourself, you understand the practical details behind compensation decisions and what it takes to implement them accurately.

You will establish how our compensation programs run: the calendar, responsibilities, systems requirements, controls, communications, and handoffs that connect program design to the employee experience. You’ll partner closely with Compensation Partners, HR Business Partners, People Operations, People Technology, Finance, Payroll, Equity Administration, and Legal, creating clarity and driving execution as priorities evolve.

In this role, you will:

  • Lead our compensation program portfolio. Own the integrated roadmap and calendar for cyclical and ad hoc programs, including compensation reviews, bonus and equity cycles, promotion-related compensation processes, recognition and retention initiatives, and new program launches.

  • Drive programs from planning through completion. Define scope, deliverables, milestones, accountable owners, dependencies, and resource needs. Coordinate work across teams, resolve blockers, and bring decisions and tradeoffs to the right owners early.

  • Translate compensation expertise into practical operations. Work with Compensation Partners and program owners to turn approved designs into clear eligibility rules, calculations, workflows, approval paths, and exception processes. Identify gaps and implementation risks before launch.

  • Stay close to the analysis and data. Build and review models, validate inputs and calculations, investigate discrepancies, and reconcile final outcomes. Be comfortable working directly in the details when a program needs it.

  • Build reliable execution controls. Establish quality checks, documented approvals, access controls, and audit trails. Coordinate accurate handoffs to Payroll, Equity Administration, and People Operations, with clear ownership through completion.

  • Shape compensation systems and tooling. Translate business needs into requirements, partner with People Technology on configuration and integrations, lead user acceptance testing, and prioritize improvements that reduce manual work and errors.

  • Manage incoming requests and changing priorities. Create a practical intake and prioritization process for ad hoc compensation initiatives. Make capacity, timing, and dependencies visible so urgent work can be delivered alongside recurring commitments.

  • Make programs easier to understand and use. Develop operating guides, manager resources, communications, and training. Equip Compensation Partners and other stakeholders to explain programs consistently and resolve questions efficiently.

  • Improve how the function operates. Measure accuracy, timeliness, manual effort, and stakeholder experience. Run post-cycle reviews and turn findings into simpler processes, stronger documentation, and effective automation.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have 10+ years of progressive compensation experience, including substantial responsibility for global compensation programs and operations in a complex, fast-growing organization.

  • Have performed the core responsibilities of a Compensation Operations Analyst, Compensation Analyst, Compensation Partner, and Compensation Program Manager, whether through separate roles or a combination of positions.

  • Bring deep compensation expertise across base pay, incentives, equity, market benchmarking, salary structures, and job architecture, and understand how these elements translate into day-to-day administration.

  • Have independently led complex compensation cycles and new initiatives, coordinating multiple teams from planning and analysis through implementation and reconciliation.

  • Are deliberately drawn to an operations-focused role. You enjoy making programs work, improving the details, and building processes that others can rely on.

  • Combine strong analytical skills with practical systems experience, including advanced spreadsheet modeling and hands-on work with Workday or comparable HR and compensation platforms.

  • Can establish priorities and drive progress when requirements are incomplete or changing, while making thoughtful tradeoffs about speed, accuracy, and capacity.

  • Communicate clearly with senior leaders and working teams, influence across functions, and make ownership and next steps explicit.

  • Exercise sound judgment with confidential information and bring a high standard of accuracy, accountability, and service to your work.

descriptionHtml:
About the team

OpenAI’s Forward Deployed Engineering team partners with life sciences organizations to deploy production AI systems across scientific and operational workflows. We work at the boundary of customer deployment and core platform development, using early engagements to define repeatable system patterns, evals, and operating standards for life sciences environments.

We are hiring a Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) to lead end-to-end deployments of our models inside life sciences organizations and research institutions, focusing on workflows across discovery, clinical development, submissions, and scientific operations. You will work with customers who are experts in their domains, translating data, infrastructure, and workflow constraints into production systems and helping define how frontier models can be applied in regulated environments.

You will measure success through production adoption, workflow impact, and eval loops that define workflow-specific benchmarks, acceptance criteria, and launch evidence for production use. You’ll work closely with Business, Research, Platform/Product, Engineering, and Security/GRC, using deployment learnings to improve both customer systems and the product and model roadmaps supporting them.

descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI’s GTM Partnerships team builds a strategic, global partner ecosystem that accelerates customer success, enables enterprise AI adoption, and drives durable growth in support of OpenAI’s mission.

Cloud partners are central to how customers discover, purchase, deploy, and scale OpenAI solutions. We work across cloud providers and their field, product, marketplace, technical, and partner organizations to reduce friction for customers and create repeatable paths from initial interest to production impact.

The team collaborates closely with Sales, Technical Success, Product, Engineering, Finance, Legal, Security, Marketing, Operations, and Customer Success to turn strategic cloud relationships into measurable customer and commercial outcomes.

About the Role

We are hiring a Partner Director, GTM Cloud Partnerships to shape and execute OpenAI’s go-to-market strategy with strategic cloud partners.

You will own senior relationships across a portfolio of cloud providers and develop joint business plans that expand customer access to OpenAI’s products, generate partner-sourced opportunities, and accelerate enterprise adoption. You will translate company-level partnerships into practical field motions spanning account planning, co-selling, cloud marketplaces, customer procurement, technical enablement, solution development, and executive engagement.

This is a highly strategic and hands-on role. Success requires executive presence, strong commercial judgment, cloud ecosystem expertise, and the operating discipline to coordinate complex initiatives across multiple partners, regions, and internal teams. The ideal candidate can move fluidly between long-term strategy and the detailed execution required to deliver measurable results.

This role is based in San Francisco, Seattle, or New York. We use a hybrid work model of three days in the office per week.

In This Role, You Will

  • Own the commercial engagement with a top global cloud partner in specific industry and customer segments, establishing strong alignment with their executive, sales, product, marketplace, technical, and partner organizations.

  • Build and run the partnership governance model for assigned customer segments, including pipeline reviews, forecasting, executive business reviews, milestone tracking, performance reporting, and escalation management.

  • Establish operating cadences for priority partnerships, including executive business reviews, pipeline inspections, forecasting, milestone tracking, performance reporting, and escalation management.

  • Identify, qualify, and accelerate partner-sourced and partner-influenced opportunities, working with OpenAI sellers to progress shared pursuits toward customer wins.

  • Develop and drive joint sales plays with cloud provider field teams and OpenAI Sales, including account mapping, joint account planning, opportunity identification, executive engagement, and deal progression.

  • Partner with Sales and Technical Success to identify, shape, and accelerate strategic enterprise opportunities involving cloud infrastructure, marketplaces, and AI transformation initiatives.

  • Collaborate with Partner Marketing on launches, campaigns, customer stories, field communications, and market-facing events.

  • Drive partner enablement across OpenAI products, use cases, technical capabilities, customer qualification, security, provisioning, and deployment best practices.

  • Represent OpenAI in executive meetings, customer engagements, strategic planning sessions, and industry events, requiring regular travel in North America. 

  • Gather structured feedback from cloud partners and customers and translate it into recommendations for OpenAI’s product, commercial, and go-to-market teams.

You Might Thrive in This Role If You Have

  • 10+ years of experience in cloud partnerships, strategic alliances, ecosystem sales, business development, or enterprise sales within cloud, SaaS, AI, or platform businesses.

  • A demonstrated track record of producing measurable pipeline, revenue, customer adoption, or marketplace outcomes through strategic partnerships.

  • Strong familiarity with cloud marketplaces, co-sell programs, committed-spend models, partner attribution, and cloud-based enterprise procurement.

  • Experience supporting complex enterprise opportunities involving AI transformation, cloud modernization, data platforms, or large-scale technical deployments.

  • The ability to build trusted relationships with senior executives while remaining close to the operational details that determine whether a partnership succeeds.

  • Technical fluency sufficient to engage credibly with cloud architects, product leaders, engineering teams, and technical decision-makers.

  • The ability to influence without formal authority, manage escalations constructively, and create urgency across internal and external teams.

  • Experience operating in an early-stage or high-growth environment where strategies, processes, and playbooks are still being built.

  • Excellent written, verbal, negotiation, and executive-presentation skills.

  • Can create structure in an ambiguous and rapidly evolving partnership landscape.

  • Combine a strategic perspective with a strong bias toward execution and measurable business outcomes.

  • Understand how cloud providers operate, from corporate strategy and product partnerships to marketplaces and field-level co-selling.

title: Visual Merchant, Hardware
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The Hardware Marketing team helps people understand what OpenAI’s hardware products can do and how they can fit into everyday life. We work with Product Marketing, Design, Creative, Sales, and Operations to bring products to market and create experiences where people can try them for themselves.

About the Role

We’re looking for a Visual Merchant to shape how customers discover, understand, and try OpenAI hardware in stores. Reporting to the Channel Lead, you’ll own visual merchandising for OpenAI-owned experiences and third-party retail. You’ll work with Creative, Design, and retail partners to build displays that tell a clear product story and make it easy for customers to get hands-on.

You’ll take the work from concept through installation, setting a standard in our own spaces and adapting it for partner stores. You’ll be as comfortable giving feedback on a prototype as you are walking a store to see what customers notice, touch, and miss.

In this role, you will:

  • Make the product story visible. Set the order in which customers see products, signage, and demos. Work with Product Marketing and Creative to keep claims accurate and give customers a clear place to start.

  • Develop visual merchandising for OpenAI experiences. Work with Design, Creative, and production partners on fixture placement, displays, signage, and hands-on demo stations. Use mockups and site visits to check sightlines, accessibility, and flow.

  • Develop the experience for global retail partners. Define what needs to stay consistent across stores and what can change for different footprints, retailer standards, and local markets. Review partner concepts, samples, and layouts before rollout.

  • Turn standards into tools store teams can use. Create layout guides, fixture and signage specifications, and setup and reset instructions. Partner with Production and Retail Operations on prototypes, installation, and quality checks so displays are safe and can be maintained day to day.

  • Use what you see in stores to improve the work. Watch how customers approach and use displays, gather feedback from store teams, and check whether installations match the brief. Use what you learn to fix issues and update the next rollout.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

  • Built visual merchandising for physical retail and can show how you took work from concept through installation. Experience with both brand-owned and partner stores is a plus.

  • Translated creative direction into practical layouts, specifications, and guides that store teams and vendors can use.

  • Worked with Creative, Design, Production, Operations, and retail partners to solve on-site issues and maintain a consistent standard across locations.

title: ITAV Event Technical Producer
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI’s IT organization supports the mission of deploying artificial general intelligence (AGI) for the benefit of all. Our team is committed to providing seamless technological support and solutions to ensure that all OpenAI employees are well-equipped and connected. This enables them to contribute effectively towards our AI research, corporate operations and product initiatives.

About the Role

As an ITAV Event Technical Producer at OpenAI, you will lead technical production for complex internal and external events across multiple sites, from early planning through rehearsal and live delivery. You will partner with internal stakeholders and technical teams to translate event requirements into clear production plans. You will coordinate internal and external crews, direct large, distributed shows and coordinate cross-site handoffs, and use your technical expertise to resolve production challenges and make informed tradeoffs. You will also build reusable production practices and AI workflows, improve how teams deliver events, and mentor peers and junior crew members.

This is a full-time, onsite role requiring five days per week in San Francisco. Travel to other OpenAI locations is required as needed for assigned events.

In this role, you will:

  • Lead technical production for complex internal, hybrid, and distributed events from early planning and scoping through rehearsal, live delivery, and debrief.

  • Align Internal Comms, Marketing, Brand Experience, and Workplace on audience goals, requirements, scope, dependencies, and decision owners. Turn ambiguous or competing needs into an agreed production plan and readiness criteria.

  • Configure and operate live audio, video switching, cameras, playback, conferencing, streaming, and recording systems for the agreed production.

  • Integrate the run of show across sites and lead multiple crews globally for all-company events. Align technical cues, rehearsals, content handoffs, schedules, and contingencies with partner teams to deliver one cohesive event.

  • Lead rehearsals and validate the complete audience experience, including remote contribution, playback, recording, and tested backup paths.

  • Independently prioritize technical production tradeoffs and lead risk reviews and incident response. Resolve ambiguity within your scope, and seek guidance for complex situations or decisions owned by event, staffing, budget, or engineering partners.

  • Build reusable production plans, show files, runbooks, and change-control practices. Coach peers and junior crew members to use them independently and verify improvements in readiness, troubleshooting, and execution.

  • Set a prioritized roadmap for production improvements using audience feedback, debriefs, and recurring failures. Lead workflow changes across teams and define permanent-system improvements with AV Engineering.

  • Identify repeatable production work and build AI and agentic workflows with partner teams. Validate results, establish operating and maintenance ownership, support adoption, and measure preparation effort or reliability improvements.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

  • Experience leading complex live or hybrid productions across multiple teams, from ambiguous requirements through rehearsal, delivery, and debrief.

  • Advanced expertise in multiple live-production domains, such as audio, video, conferencing, streaming, or AV-over-IP, and the ability to diagnose complex interactions across the complete signal path.

  • Experience configuring and operating professional production systems and creating reusable show files or control workflows.

  • Practical AV-over-IP and networking knowledge sufficient to troubleshoot live media, timing, and connectivity with engineering partners.

  • Experience independently resolving ambiguous production problems, setting detailed plans, and prioritizing tradeoffs while seeking guidance when complexity or decision authority requires it.

  • Demonstrated ownership of rehearsals, technical readiness, failover testing, and calm incident response for high-priority productions.

  • Ability to lead crews and influence partner teams without reporting authority, with clear boundaries for content, brand, budget, staffing, and engineering decisions.

  • Experience working with communications, marketing, brand or creative experience, Workplace, and technical partners on complex events, including sensitive planning and late changes.

  • Experience building reusable production frameworks and validated AI workflows, guiding team adoption, and mentoring peers or junior staff with measurable improvements in their capability.

  • Experience with multi-space or multi-location productions and sensitive executive events is a plus.

  • Experience with systems such as Q-SYS, Dante, Ross, Vizrt, or comparable production platforms is a plus.

About the Team

The Strategic Finance team partners across OpenAI to turn company strategy into financial decisions, help allocate resources, and steer the business toward its highest-impact long-term outcomes.

Within Strategic Finance, the B2B Product Finance team owns the financial perspective on growth across OpenAI’s B2B portfolio. We connect monetization and customer economics with compute demand, capacity, margin, and resource planning, partnering closely with Product, GTM, Strategic Deal Desk, Compute Finance, Capacity Planning, Data, Accounting, and other Finance teams.

We are hiring a strategic finance partner to partner with Product and GTM leaders in incubating and launching new B2B Products. You will evaluate new product initiatives and commercial viability, help shape commercial strategy, develop forecasts and revenue targets, and build the 0→1 financial foundations and decision-making frameworks to scale these products. 

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

title: Sales Manager, Global Ads Solutions - Travel
descriptionHtml:
About the team

The Global Ad Solutions team helps businesses connect with people in useful, relevant ways through OpenAI’s advertising products. We partner with advertisers and agencies to understand their goals, build effective strategies, and demonstrate the value of our platform, while putting the user experience and trust at the center of everything we do.

We are building an advertising business from the ground up. That means working across Sales, Product, Marketing, Measurement and Operations to solve new problems, shape how we go to market, and help our customers grow alongside us.

About the role

We’re looking for a Sales Manager to build, lead and develop a high-performing team of Client Partners and Customer Success Managers serving airlines, hotels, online travel agencies, tourism boards, cruise lines and other travel brands. You’ll own your team’s revenue performance, customer relationships and execution, while helping define the sales practices and culture that will enable our business to scale.

You are a hands-on leader who can coach through a complex customer conversation, build an actionable plan from data, and bring clarity and focus in a fast-changing environment. You balance near-term results with long-term customer partnerships and make thoughtful decisions that protect user trust.

You’ll coach the team to build advertising partnerships that help people discover destinations, compare options and plan trips. You’ll help advertisers connect campaigns to goals such as bookings, destination awareness and loyalty program growth.

In this role, you will:

  • Hire, coach and develop a diverse team of Client Partners and Customer Success Managers, providing clear expectations, regular feedback and opportunities for growth.

  • Own the team’s revenue and business objectives, planning pipeline and account coverage around seasonal booking windows, new routes or properties, and year-round advertiser priorities.

  • Establish a consistent operating rhythm for account reviews, forecasting and prioritization, using data to identify risks, opportunities and actions.

  • Coach Client Partners and Customer Success Managers on executive relationships, complex negotiations and account plans that connect launch or seasonal campaigns to longer-term customer goals.

  • Build senior relationships with key advertisers and agencies, serving as an executive partner and escalation point when needed.

  • Partner closely with Agency, Marketing Science, Solutions Engineering and Product to help advertisers measure outcomes across the travel planning journey, from destination discovery to booking.

  • Bring customer and market insights back to internal teams, helping shape product priorities, sales strategy and go-to-market execution.

  • Develop repeatable tools, processes and best practices that improve how the team works as the business grows.

  • Foster a culture of ownership, collaboration, candor and continuous learning, while upholding OpenAI’s commitment to user trust and responsible growth.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have 10+ years of experience in digital advertising, media, marketing solutions or a related client-facing commercial role, including 3+ years leading and developing sales teams.

  • Have a track record of building or growing teams and delivering against ambitious revenue goals in a dynamic environment.

  • Are an effective coach who can develop people with different strengths, provide direct and constructive feedback, and create an inclusive, high-accountability team culture.

  • Have experience advising senior travel advertisers and their agencies on investment decisions shaped by seasonality, booking windows and loyalty goals.

  • Understand how travel advertisers evaluate brand and performance campaigns using measures such as destination awareness, bookings and loyalty program sign-ups.

  • Use data to prioritize opportunities, inspect a pipeline, improve forecast quality and turn insights into clear action.

title: Lab Operations Engineer, Systems Integration | Consumer Devices
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI Consumer Devices is building the next generation of products that bring powerful AI into people’s everyday lives. Guided by OpenAI’s mission to ensure AGI benefits all of humanity, our team combines world-class researchers, engineers, designers, and operators who care deeply about creating useful, intuitive, and responsible technology. You’ll have the opportunity to work alongside exceptional people on ambitious, zero-to-one challenges at the intersection of hardware, software, and AI. This is a chance to help define an entirely new category of products—and shape how people experience AI in the future.

The Systems Integration team is critical in this mission, turning complex hardware-software development into reliable product signals. Lab Operations is the physical backbone of that work: we build and maintain the device fleets, test environments, and hardware-in-the-loop labs that let teams test repeatably, understand failures, and ship with confidence.

About the Role

As a Lab Operations Manager, Systems Integration, you will own the day-to-day operation of a large-scale consumer device test lab. This is a hands-on operations leadership role: you’ll keep device fleets, test rigs, lab infrastructure, inventory, provisioning, maintenance, and logistics running smoothly so engineers and QA technicians have reliable environments for validation and release testing.

We’re looking for someone who is highly organized, technically hands-on, comfortable with consumer electronics and lab equipment, and experienced operating complex physical test environments at scale. Because this is a new category of devices, you’ll have the opportunity to build the lab operating model early—shaping the systems, standards, and workflows that support products from prototype through launch.

In this role, you will:

  • Own device fleet and inventory: Manage configuration, deployment, tracking, lifecycle, and accurate asset records for a large fleet of consumer devices and test equipment; coordinate receiving, storage, checkout, shipping, transfers, spares, and secure disposal.

  • Operate and maintain the lab: Keep racks, benches, test rigs, cabling, power, networking, peripherals, and shared equipment reliable and organized; diagnose issues and coordinate repairs, replacements, and preventive maintenance.

  • Prepare devices for testing: Flash, provision, reset, configure, label, and assign devices to test environments.

  • Support testing and diagnostics: Partner with engineering and QA on large-scale test automation setups, failure reproduction, diagnostics collection, log capture, and environment resets.

  • Plan lab readiness and capacity: Track fleet health, rig availability, utilization, and upcoming test needs; identify constraints before they block testing.

  • Partner across teams: Work with hardware, systems, QA, reliability, IT, and infrastructure teams to keep the lab ready for development and release activities.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Proven track-record of operating or supporting a hardware, electronics, reliability, manufacturing, or QA test lab.

  • Hands-on experience managing fleets of consumer electronics, embedded devices, prototypes, or connected hardware.

  • Comfortable setting up, configuring, troubleshooting, and maintaining devices, test rigs, networking, power systems, and peripherals across USB, Wi-Fi, Ethernet, Bluetooth, power, and device connectivity.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have strong organizational skills and can manage competing requests while keeping inventory, asset tracking, maintenance records, lab logistics, and shared spaces documented and operational.

  • Are comfortable following technical procedures for provisioning, firmware installation, resets, diagnostics collection, and test setup.

  • Communicate clearly with engineers, QA teams, vendors, and technicians and are comfortable escalating issues with concise supporting information.

  • Enjoy improving the reliability, scalability, and efficiency of physical lab operations.

title: Hardware Systems Planning Lead (1P)
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI’s 1P Hardware Systems team operates at the intersection of Hardware Engineering, Infrastructure, Supply Chain, Manufacturing, Deployment, and Finance to translate infrastructure demand into an executable systems plan.

The Planning Lead connects system demand and deployment timing to site and configuration requirements, power availability, XPU needs, hardware supply commitments, manufacturing capacity, and site readiness.

About the Role

OpenAI is seeking a 1P Hardware Systems Planning Lead to own the integrated demand, supply, and deployment plan for our 1P AI infrastructure systems. This role will connect infrastructure demand and site power availability to system configurations, XPU requirements, and hardware supply commitments—creating a single, actionable view of whether our deployment plan can be met.

You will establish the planning mechanisms that allow teams to see what changed, understand the impact, and act quickly when demand, supply, configuration, site readiness, or power timing moves. You will work across Hardware Engineering, Infrastructure, Supply Chain, Strategic Sourcing, Manufacturing, Deployment, and Finance to identify gaps early and drive recovery plans to closure.

This is a highly cross-functional role for someone who combines systems-level thinking, strong analytical judgment, and rigorous program execution. The ideal candidate can turn complex and changing inputs into a clear operating plan, surface the decisions that matter, and drive accountability across teams without relying on formal authority. Success also requires strong communication judgment: the ability to align cross-functional teams, brief leadership at a concise and decision-oriented level, and go deep into the underlying assumptions, dependencies, risks, and recovery plans when needed.

Responsibilities

  • Integrated Planning - Own the integrated planning process for 1P hardware systems, connecting system demand, deployment timing, site and configuration requirements, power availability, XPU needs, and supply commitments.

  • Maintain a clear, decision-ready supply plan that shows changes from the prior plan; weekly pull-ins and push-outs; site, deployment, and system-configuration impacts; power availability assumptions and timing; system demand and corresponding XPU requirements; current supplier and manufacturing commitments; gaps between forecast, requirements, and committed supply; and recovery actions with accountable owners and target closure dates.

  • Validate that the end-to-end supply plan is executable, including the timing and dependencies across components, XPU availability, system integration, factory capacity, site readiness, and deployment.

  • Operating Cadence & Change Management - Lead a weekly deployment and supply review focused on material changes, emerging risks, required decisions, and recovery-plan execution.

  • Publish and maintain a weekly delta report that clearly explains what changed, why it changed, and the downstream impact to deployments, sites, configurations, power, and supply.

  • Track forecast-versus-commit gaps at a weekly level, identify the underlying constraints, and drive recovery plans with named owners and dates.

  • Coordinate the biweekly end-to-end supply picture update for leadership and key stakeholders, including the latest system forecast; how the forecast aligns with site power availability and timing; current supply commitments; weekly gaps to commit; and the plan and timing to close each gap.

  • Cross-Functional Execution & Risk Management - Partner with Hardware Engineering and Infrastructure teams to translate roadmap, configuration, and deployment changes into updated system and XPU requirements.

  • Work through the Supply Chain team to pressure-test commitments with manufacturing partners and suppliers, understand constraints, and establish credible recovery paths.

  • Anticipate supply and deployment risks, develop scenarios and tradeoffs, and provide crisp recommendations to senior leaders.

  • Process & Operational Scaling - Build scalable planning models, reporting standards, and operating mechanisms that improve forecast accuracy, change control, traceability, and executive decision-making as 1P infrastructure scales.

Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications

  • Significant experience in hardware systems planning, supply planning, program management, operations, or a related role supporting complex, high-volume technology products or infrastructure.

  • Strong understanding of the dependencies among hardware demand, component supply, manufacturing capacity, system configurations, site readiness, power availability, and deployment schedules.

  • Experience building and managing integrated demand-and-supply plans at weekly granularity, including forecast changes, supply commits, gaps, scenarios, and recovery actions.

  • Demonstrated ability to pressure-test whether a plan is executable rather than simply consolidating inputs from different teams.

  • Exceptional analytical skills and the ability to translate complex datasets and technical dependencies into clear insights, decisions, and actions.

  • Strong program leadership, including experience establishing operating cadences, driving cross-functional accountability, and closing issues across organizations.

  • Demonstrated experience communicating effectively across cross-functional teams and with senior leadership, with the judgment to tailor the level of detail to the audience—distilling complex issues into concise, decision-ready updates while going deep on assumptions, dependencies, risks, and recovery plans when needed.

  • Comfortable operating in a fast-moving, high-ambiguity environment where requirements, priorities, and constraints evolve quickly.

  • High ownership, sound judgment, and a bias toward surfacing risks early and driving them through resolution.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with AI infrastructure, hyperscale data centers, or accelerator systems.

  • Experience with semiconductors, server or rack manufacturing, or complex hardware supply chains.

What Success Looks Like

  • A single, trusted view of 1P hardware system demand, supply commitments, deployment timing, and associated gaps.

  • Clear weekly visibility into changes, pull-ins, push-outs, and their impact on sites, configurations, power, systems, and XPUs.

  • Early identification of risks to the deployment plan, with quantified impact and actionable recovery paths.

  • Work through SCPM and strategic sourcing to ensure every material gap has a clear recovery plan, accountable owner, target date, and escalation path.

  • Forecast, supply, manufacturing, site-readiness, and power assumptions remain aligned across teams.

  • Leadership receives a concise, consistent, and decision-oriented biweekly view of the end-to-end supply picture.

  • Planning processes and tools scale with the pace, volume, and complexity of OpenAI’s 1P infrastructure roadmap.

The Strategic Finance team provides financial insights and guidance to support the organization's long-term goals and strategies. We partner across the business to allocate and deploy our resources for the highest impact outcomes.

About the Role

Our Workloads team under Research focuses on maximizing the performance and efficiency of model inference, enabling OpenAI to develop and deploy frontier AI models at scale.
